Only in Muarihu to the prefect: you bought back my slaves for 400 silver from Hehea the Egyptian; you swore in the house of the gods; give me their ransom silver and the rest, let there be no debt between us, we are one man (RS 15.0011): A creditor asks that the account be settled so that there be no debt between the two, 'for we are one man'; A slave redeemed (released for silver) from foreigners is sent back to his master, with a plea that no bad word come between the two rulers.

Only in Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform: The king kneels on a bronze platform in the court and spreads his hands to heaven; People away from Jerusalem or in exile pray in the direction of the land, city and temple; Captives confess in exile 'We have sinned, done wrong and acted wickedly'; 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and the ark of your might'; Prayer lists famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, siege and sickness as occasions for prayer; A foreigner from a far land who hears of God's name comes to pray at the temple and is heard; 'There is no man who does not sin'; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; 'O my servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; God forgives all sins'; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts]; and 7 more.

Only in The witness gods, with the gods of Wiluša and Appaliuna (CTH 76 §§20-23): A god [A]ppaliuna (possibly Apollo) is named among the gods of Wiluša (perhaps Troy) invoked as treaty witnesses; The underground watercourses (KASKAL.KUR, sinkholes) of a land are invoked among the treaty witnesses; Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; The sun god is shepherd of the land and father of the black-headed; A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty.

Only in Shalmaneser I of Assyria to Ibiranu of Ugarit: Tudhaliya of Hatti sent tablets of war and of peace, refused to return fugitives or to touch the oath-tablet before the Sun; at Nihriya I entered the Hittite army and made a great slaughter (RSO 07, 046): A king asks why we, who are brothers, are enemies to one another; An enemy king's messenger carries two tablets of hostility and one of peace, showing whichever suits the situation; A herald cries to the camp: put on your coats of mail and mount your chariots, the enemy king is drawn up and coming; Challenged to touch a tablet of oath before the sun god to prove his peaceful intent, a king refuses; The king boasts in the first person of how he crushes the enemy: foot on their neck, blood, nets, weapons; The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it; Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back.

Only in Ḫatiya's ritual for the demoness Wišuriyant at the river (CTH 396.1.1 §1-6): The demoness Wišuriyant (the 'strangler') is brought down to the river, a tent set up, and she is washed with clay of the bank: 'see, I have purified you'; A fish with a cake in its mouth is released into the river to go to the mountain and the river and bring the offering to the demoness; The fish is thrown on the hearth and burned, and there is no smoke; Three pits are dug before the river bank and breads broken for the fate goddesses and the mother goddess, who are asked for life, health, vigour, long years and sight; The deity is asked to give the patient life, health, vigour, long years and the sight of the eyes; The Sun god of heaven is called as witness of the offering: if the demoness hides anything, you shall know it; The ritualist sets food and drink before the angry god and invokes him (mugai-): eat, drink, still your hunger and thirst, come back and be at peace.

Über Rasur. Die Lücke am Anfang von Vs. 6' reicht für ca. 8 Zeichen, von denen ein Teil auf das Prädikat des vorausgehenden Kolons entfällt. Lesungsvorschlag von Del Monte 1981, 218 (gegen seine ältere Auffassung als Ortsname in Del Monte-Tischler 1978, 371); so auch Beckman 1999, 26 und CHD P, 5b. Da -wa nicht die Partikel der direkten Rede sein kann, hat man es wohl als irreguläre Stützsilbe zwischen -ŠU und -aš zu betrachten. Für eine weitere ungewöhnliche Graphie in diesem Text s. KUR-e-TAM in Vs. 3'. Man beachte die Abwesenheit der scriptio plena. Die Autographie in KUB 36 bietet vor der Lücke ein AŠ (Del Monte 1981, 215 liest na-aš [ ), aber nach Foto scheint diese Lesung schwierig; das beschädigte Zeichen ist vielleicht besser als -a[m- zu lesen. Das Kolon ist von dem folgenden durch einen schrägen Keil getrennt. Der Paralleltext KBo 19.39 + KUB 8.81 (CTH 41.II.1) trennt die entsprechenden Kola in Vs. II 4'-5' durch einen Abschnittsstrich. Dies könnte auf eine nachträgliche Einfügung hinweisen. Für die Emendation <Ú-UL> nach der Parallele KUB 8.81+ Rs. III 3 s. schon Petschow 1963, 244 Anm. 40. evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust (weight 6.6); Madness, blindness and confusion; groping at noon like the blind in darkness (weight 6.5); Locust, worm and cricket devour crops, vines and trees (weight 6.5). Pair score 19.6.

Only in SAA 2 2 iii-vi: Matiʾ-il's obligations, curses (famine, cannibalism, prostitutes, mule) and the divine witnesses: Curse: may a city of a thousand houses be reduced to one house, a thousand tents to one, one man left in the city; Curse: may the dung of oxen, donkeys, sheep and horses not be found in the land (livestock wiped out); Curse: may the oath-breaker's soldiers become women and take payment like prostitutes in the city square; may the war goddess take away their bow; The punished cry 'woe (ahula / yā waylanā), we have sinned (been wrongdoers)'; Curse: may dust be their food, pitch their ointment, donkey's urine their drink, papyrus their clothing, a hole their bed; Curse: may the oath-breaker's life be like a mule's (sterile) and his wife reach extreme old age (childless); Warriors come 'with a whole heart', 'not with a double heart', with one heart to make the king; Curse: may the moon god clothe the oath-breaker in skin disease (saharšubbû) like a garment, so that he roams the open country; Curse: may the war goddess make the oath-breaker kneel or sit bound at the feet of his enemy; Destruction undoes fertility: brackish water in rivers, weeds in fields, no lambs in the fold, no churning song; Curse: you will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters; Curse: may the gods break the oath-breaker's sceptre and overthrow his kingship; and 4 more.

Only in Blessings and the great curses: Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough; Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb; Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege; Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways; King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone; As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you; God will make you the head and not the tail; God puts an iron yoke on your neck; God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy; The stranger in your midst rises higher and higher while you sink; Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed; Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; and 18 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed (weight 6.1); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 11.0.

Only in SAA 2 8: Zakūtu (Naqiʾa), queen mother, imposes a loyalty oath for her grandson Ashurbanipal: The queen mother herself imposes a loyalty oath on the royal family and the whole land in favour of her grandson the king; If the sworn party hears of a plot to kill the king, or of men inciting revolt among courtiers, kin or the people, he must report it and seize and kill the plotters; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed (weight 6.1); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.6.

Only in SAA 2 9: Loyalty oath of Babylonian allies to Ashurbanipal after Šamaš-šuma-ukīn's revolt: Curse: may the god uproot the oath-breaker above among the living and deprive his ghost of water below in the earth; Curse: may the high god decree for the oath-breaker a reign of sighing, few days and years of want; Any letter or messenger arriving from the enemy or a foreign land must be seized and sent on to the king; Curse: may the war goddess make the oath-breaker kneel or sit bound at the feet of his enemy; Madness, blindness and confusion; groping at noon like the blind in darkness; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; The servant declares: 'Whatever my lord says, I will do'; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.5.

Only in SAA 2 9: Loyalty oath of Babylonian allies to Ashurbanipal after Šamaš-šuma-ukīn's revolt: Curse: may the god uproot the oath-breaker above among the living and deprive his ghost of water below in the earth; Curse: may the high god decree for the oath-breaker a reign of sighing, few days and years of want; Any letter or messenger arriving from the enemy or a foreign land must be seized and sent on to the king; Curse: may the war goddess make the oath-breaker kneel or sit bound at the feet of his enemy; Madness, blindness and confusion; groping at noon like the blind in darkness; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The servant declares: 'Whatever my lord says, I will do'; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy.

Only in Rumours of revolt, 'come alone', no bird oracle, campaigns and the great kings (CTH 76 §§10-14): When summoned to help the king, the vassal must not first take a bird oracle; Taking or reading an omen from birds is set aside; The oath is broken if the vassal hears of sedition and overlooks it, saying 'let that evil happen'; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy (weight 6.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Only in SAA 2 13: Treaty with an Arab ruler: no peace with the enemy, no secret messages, report every hostile word: The sworn party must not send messages secretly, 'whether by the hand of a fish of the sea or a bird of the sky'; The vassal is bound to fear the overlord and do what is good for him; Forbidden: sending secret messages to the overlord's (God's) enemy.

Only in Šunaššura treaty, Hittite version (CTH 41.II.2): Mittani, help 'if it suits him', fugitives, wife and children as compensation: Whoever hides a fugitive in his house must give twelve persons in compensation, or himself be killed; a hiding slave's master may forfeit him; An oath by YHWH settles a dispute without witnesses; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it (weight 6.8); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 (Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty, Tayinat copy) i: seals of Aššur, parties, future generations, divine witnesses: An oath or covenant that binds descendants not yet born [divergence between the texts]; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; A loyalty oath (adê) is imposed by the Assyrian king (or queen mother) on vassals or subjects, binding them to him and his heir 'from this day as long as we live'; The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people.

Only in Alakšandu's chosen son, mutual protection, the fugitive conspirator (CTH 76 §§6-9): If the vassal's brother or kin rebels and seeks the throne, the overlord will recognise only the vassal, not accept the rebel, and destroy the rebel's land; The overlord promises that the son the vassal will beget shall be king after him and shall be protected as his father is; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet: Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him; The sworn must not perform a rite to undo the oath (anointing with tallow from the gods, binding something on the thigh, 'turning back' or 'releasing' the oath); An oath or profession spoken with the lips (tongues) only, not with the whole heart; The sworn must take the oath with their whole heart, not with the lips only, and teach it to their sons who come after; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them; The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words.

Only in Protect the king's line; do not act like Mašturi; be ready to die (CTH 105 §§5-9): A vassal betrays his benefactor's son, asking 'shall I protect a bastard?', and is held up in a later treaty as a warning; The great king takes the vassal by the hand, gives him his sister in marriage, makes him his brother-in-law and king of his land; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it (weight 6.8); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 v: the prince's brothers, succession at the king's death, no annulment rites, whole-hearted oath taught to sons, the sealed tablet: Formula: in future days the national god is 'your god' and the crown prince 'your lord'; your sons and grandsons shall fear him; The sworn must not perform a rite to undo the oath (anointing with tallow from the gods, binding something on the thigh, 'turning back' or 'releasing' the oath); An oath or profession spoken with the lips (tongues) only, not with the whole heart; The sworn must take the oath with their whole heart, not with the lips only, and teach it to their sons who come after; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; Command not to add to or subtract from the divine words; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in Alakšandu's chosen son, mutual protection, the fugitive conspirator (CTH 76 §§6-9): If the vassal's brother or kin rebels and seeks the throne, the overlord will recognise only the vassal, not accept the rebel, and destroy the rebel's land; The overlord promises that the son the vassal will beget shall be king after him and shall be protected as his father is; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy.

Only in SAA 2 15 v-vi: curses god by god (Aššur to Kubaba): disease, leprosy, famine and cannibalism, unburied corpses, darkness: In the morning you will say: would it were evening; in the evening: would it were morning; Curse: may the gods eradicate his name and seed from the land and give his flesh to the mouth of dogs; Curse: may the god turn the oath-breaker's land into a flood-ruin mound and his cities into tells; Curse: as the worm eats stored food, may worms eat your flesh while you are alive; may a goddess make a worm come out of your belly; Curse: may the high god decree for the oath-breaker a reign of sighing, few days and years of want; The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient; The blood of the slain is splashed on the ground like a rainstorm; The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: curses by the gods one by one (SAA 2 6:414-493): Treaty curses invoke western gods (Bethel, Anath-Bethel, Kubaba of Carchemish, Aramiš) alongside the Assyrian pantheon; Curse: may the sky god rain illness, exhaustion, headache, sleeplessness and wailing on all your houses; Curse: may an irresistible flood come up from the earth and devastate you; Curse: may the goddess show you no mercy or favour; Curse: may the high god not grant long days, old age and extreme old age; A punishment (skin disease; hunger and fear) put on the guilty like a garment; Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed; Curse: may a foreign enemy divide the oath-breaker's possessions; Curse: may the storm god withhold rain from heaven and flood from the deep, and the wise god dam the rivers at their source; The god titled 'light of heaven(s) and earth' (nūr šamāmī u qaqqari / nūru l-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ), and those deprived of light walk in darkness; God will uproot the wicked from the land of the living; Futility curse: betroth a wife another lies with, build a house and not live in it, plant a vineyard and not enjoy it; and 1 more.

Only in SAA 2 15 v-vi: curses god by god (Aššur to Kubaba): disease, leprosy, famine and cannibalism, unburied corpses, darkness: Curse: may the birth goddess cut off birth in the land, and the nurse be deprived of the cry of a baby in the street; Curse: may your days be dark and your years years of darkness that never brightens; Curse: may evil demons (šēdu, utukku, rābiṣu) choose your houses as their dwelling; Curse: may there be no sound of the grindstone or the oven in your houses; Curse: may dust be their food, pitch their ointment, donkey's urine their drink, papyrus their clothing, a hole their bed; Curse: may the gods eradicate his name and seed from the land and give his flesh to the mouth of dogs; Curse: may the gods (Bethel and Anat-Bethel) hand the oath-breaker over to a man-eating lion; Curse: may the god turn the oath-breaker's land into a flood-ruin mound and his cities into tells; Curse: in famine the mother bars her door against her own daughter; you eat the flesh of your sons, grind their bones instead of grain; man eats man and wears his skin; Curse: may the plague god finish off the oath-breaker's people with blows and pestilence; Curse: may your corpses find no burial; may dogs and pigs (or eagle and jackal) eat your flesh, their bellies your grave; Curse: as the worm eats stored food, may worms eat your flesh while you are alive; may a goddess make a worm come out of your belly; and 9 more.

Only in Blessings and the great curses: Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough; Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb; Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege; Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways; King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone; As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you; God will make you the head and not the tail; God puts an iron yoke on your neck; God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy; The stranger in your midst rises higher and higher while you sink; Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed; Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; and 15 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 vi: the sworn speak: 'if we rebel, make terms with his enemy, or conceal sedition': If the sworn party hears of a plot to kill the king, or of men inciting revolt among courtiers, kin or the people, he must report it and seize and kill the plotters; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy.

Only in Protect the king's line; do not act like Mašturi; be ready to die (CTH 105 §§5-9): A vassal betrays his benefactor's son, asking 'shall I protect a bastard?', and is held up in a later treaty as a warning; The great king takes the vassal by the hand, gives him his sister in marriage, makes him his brother-in-law and king of his land; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 10.2.

Only in SAA 2 15 vi: the sworn speak: 'if we rebel, make terms with his enemy, or conceal sedition': If the sworn party hears of a plot to kill the king, or of men inciting revolt among courtiers, kin or the people, he must report it and seize and kill the plotters; The king makes all the lands swear by the great gods to accept his two sons, one as crown prince of Assyria and one of Babylon, and protect their thrones; The vassal must not make peace or come to terms ('put his mouth') with the overlord's enemy.

Only in Treaty of Šuppiluliuma I with Ḫuqqana of Ḫayaša (CTH 42) §1-6: the last dog, the sister given, 'recognize only me', love as your own soul: The overlord says he took up the vassal as 'the last dog' and treated him well; The overlord gives his sister or daughter in marriage to the vassal king; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Simile curse: as tin cannot stand before fire, so may you not stand before your enemy (weight 7.7); Curse: may the sun god overturn your city, land and district with an iron plough (weight 7.7); Simile curse: as this bug stinks, may your breath stink before god, king and mankind (weight 7.7); Curse: may your flesh and your family's be blackened like pitch, bitumen and naphtha (weight 7.7); Curse: may your rivers and springs make their water flow backward (weight 7.7); Curse: may bread be bought for its weight in gold in your land (weight 7.7); Simile curse: as the caterpillar does not return to its cocoon, so may you not return to your wives and houses (weight 7.7); Curse: as the worm eats stored food, may worms eat your flesh while you are alive; may a goddess make a worm come out of your belly (weight 7.3); Curse: may the oath-breaker's life be like a mule's (sterile) and his wife reach extreme old age (childless) (weight 7.3); Curse: may your brothers and sons chase and kill you like a stag; may you be bitter to each other like gall; may they strangle you (weight 7.1); Simile curse: as bread and wine enter the intestines, or oil penetrates flesh, so may this oath enter your body and your children's (weight 7.1); The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust (weight 6.6); Curse: may the war goddess break the oath-breaker's bow in fierce battle (weight 6.5); Locust, worm and cricket devour crops, vines and trees (weight 6.5). Pair score 102.6.

Only in SAA 2 15 vii: further curses and simile curses (bronze sky, mule's seed, iron plough, ewe and lambs, oath entering the body): Treaty enactment: an animal brought not for sacrifice but for the oath is dismembered with the words 'this head is not the lamb's head, it is the head of X'; as it is cut, so may the oath-breaker be; Curse: in famine the mother bars her door against her own daughter; you eat the flesh of your sons, grind their bones instead of grain; man eats man and wears his skin; Curse: may the scribe god who bears the tablet of fates erase your name and destroy your seed from the land; Curse: may the sun god cast his bronze bird-snare and inescapable net over you and not let you out; Curse: may your corpses find no burial; may dogs and pigs (or eagle and jackal) eat your flesh, their bellies your grave; The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient; Simile curse: 'just as this (object, animal, wax figure, ewe, water-skin) is treated, so may it be done to you'.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: analogical and simile curses I: iron earth and bronze sky to the stinking bug (SAA 2 6:526-611): Curse: as honey is sweet, may the blood of your wives and children be sweet in your mouth; Simile curse: as these lambs are slit and their entrails rolled round their feet, so may yours and your children's be; Simile curse: may your flesh and your family's be consumed like the flesh of a chameleon; Simile curse: as a honeycomb is pierced with holes, may holes be bored in your flesh while you live; Curse: may you be like a fly in the hand of your enemy, who crushes you; Simile curse: as snake and mongoose do not share a hole but plot each other's death, may husband and wife not share house or bed; Curse: instead of rain may burning coals rain on your land; Simile curse enacted with an object or animal: 'just as this X is ..., so may you be ...'; Simile curse: as a wax figure burns in fire and a clay figure dissolves in water, so may your form be burned and sink; Simile curse: as malt in the mash does not sprout, may your seed vanish from the land; The king catches fleeing enemies like gazelles, wild asses, fish or birds in nets and traps; Curse: you will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters; and 1 more.

יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת מְטַ֥ר אַרְצְךָ֖ אָבָ֣ק וְעָפָ֑ר מִן הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ יֵרֵ֣ד עָלֶ֔יךָ עַ֖ד הִשָּׁמְדָֽךְ

passages.text: זֶ֥רַע רַ֖ב תּוֹצִ֣יא הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּמְעַ֣ט תֶּאֱסֹ֔ף כִּ֥י יַחְסְלֶ֖נּוּ הָאַרְבֶּֽה
כְּרָמִ֥ים תִּטַּ֖ע וְעָבָ֑דְתָּ וְיַ֤יִן לֹֽא תִשְׁתֶּה֙ וְלֹ֣א תֶאֱגֹ֔ר כִּ֥י תֹאכְלֶ֖נּוּ הַתֹּלָֽעַת
זֵיתִ֛ים יִהְי֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּכָל גְּבוּלֶ֑ךָ וְשֶׁ֨מֶן֙ לֹ֣א תָס֔וּךְ כִּ֥י יִשַּׁ֖ל זֵיתֶֽךָ

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The evil diseases of Egypt removed from the obedient or brought on the disobedient (weight 6.8); The sky over you bronze and the earth under you iron; rain turned to dust (weight 6.6); Locust, worm and cricket devour crops, vines and trees (weight 6.5). Pair score 20.0.

Only in SAA 2 15 vii: further curses and simile curses (bronze sky, mule's seed, iron plough, ewe and lambs, oath entering the body): Curse: may bread be bought for its weight in gold in your land; Simile curse: as this bug stinks, may your breath stink before god, king and mankind; Curse: may the sun god overturn your city, land and district with an iron plough; Curse: may your flesh and your family's be blackened like pitch, bitumen and naphtha; Simile curse: as tin cannot stand before fire, so may you not stand before your enemy; Simile curse: as the caterpillar does not return to its cocoon, so may you not return to your wives and houses; Curse: may your rivers and springs make their water flow backward; Treaty enactment: an animal brought not for sacrifice but for the oath is dismembered with the words 'this head is not the lamb's head, it is the head of X'; as it is cut, so may the oath-breaker be; Curse: in famine the mother bars her door against her own daughter; you eat the flesh of your sons, grind their bones instead of grain; man eats man and wears his skin; Curse: may the scribe god who bears the tablet of fates erase your name and destroy your seed from the land; Curse: may the oath-breaker's life be like a mule's (sterile) and his wife reach extreme old age (childless); Curse: may the sun god cast his bronze bird-snare and inescapable net over you and not let you out; and 6 more.

Only in Blessings and the great curses: Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough; Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb; Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege; Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways; King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone; As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you; God will make you the head and not the tail; God puts an iron yoke on your neck; God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy; The stranger in your midst rises higher and higher while you sink; Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed; Have you seen what you sow? Do you make it grow, or are we the grower? We could make it chaff; and 18 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The sworn speak in the first person ('if we ...') and call on the named gods to seek out their seed if they rebel (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: the vassals' first-person oath and further curses by Aššur, Palil, Ea, Girra (SAA 2 6:494-525): Curse: may water and oil become taboo to you; Curse: may the god of the deep give you water of death to drink and fill you with dropsy; Curse: may the oath-breakers' seed and images be burned in fire and their torch extinguished in water; Your corpse food for birds and beasts with no one to frighten them away; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

Only in CTH 52.I §11-12: the gods of Mittani; Šattiwazza and the Hurrians curse themselves - tamarisk, water of the gutter, smoke, salt; their blessing in the lord's shade: Self-curse: as salt has no seed, so may we have no seed; like a dissolved lump of salt may we not be restored; Self-curse: as a felled tree (tamarisk/acacia) puts out no shoot, so may we have no seed; Self-curse: may we rise like smoke to heaven; The vassal asks that the great king love him and his land as he loves his own lands, sons and his own tablet; The sworn people pray to eat a rich harvest in their lord's shade (ṣillu) while he goes before them; Mitra, Varuna, Indra and the Nāsatyas are invoked as witnesses of a Mittani treaty; Mortality likened to water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up; Treaty blessing: may the land be restored as of old, grow rich and lie down (rabāṣu) in peace; Treaty curse: may the gods overturn your throne; The vassal may keep concubines but may take no wife above or equal to the overlord's sister or daughter, who must be chief wife; The people and lands relax under the king's broad protection (an-dul3, 'shade'); Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed (weight 6.1); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.6.

Only in Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty: fight a usurper; resist incitement to set the prince against his father and brothers (SAA 2 6:302-372): The treaty quotes the envious instigators' persuasive speech ('where is what the gods said about him? ... guard your lives') to forbid it; Jealous brothers spread slander and falsehood against the chosen heir and turn the father's heart against him; The sworn must protect the crown prince's brothers, not slander them before him, nor change the positions their father assigned them.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God's righteousness will be told to a people yet unborn (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Assurbanipal's hymn to Aššur (SAA 3 1): The god is creator of those of heaven and earth, fashioner of the mountains and creator of the gods; A hymn opens with the singer's resolve: 'let me magnify the god, make his greatness manifest, extol his name'; A deity is 'wide of ear' and knows everything; All the Igigi kneel before the god and the Anunnaki praise his name from their sanctuaries; The warrior god (Ninurta, or Nabû in commentary) defeats and kills the Anzu bird; The god's ingenuity is like tangled threads no eye can follow; he is his own counsellor and no one comprehends his deeds; 'Who can change the word that An, the king, has spoken?': the high god's decree cannot be altered; 'Who can change the word that has gone out?' / 'none can change his words'.

Only in Psalm 22 - my God, my God, why have you forsaken me: The emaciated sufferer can count all his bones while enemies stare; Even those who go down to the dust (the dead) will bow before God; All the ends of the earth and families of the nations will remember and turn to YHWH and bow; Dogs and a band of evildoers surround the sufferer; Appeal to the ancestors: our fathers trusted in you and you delivered them; The enemies divide the sufferer's garments among them and cast lots for his clothing; God is holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel; Crux 'like a lion my hands and my feet' (ka'ari), read by others as 'they pierced my hands and feet'; Rescue from the lion's mouth and the horns of the wild oxen; The sufferer calls himself a worm and not a man, scorned by people; Onlookers mock, wag their heads and say 'He trusted in YHWH; let him rescue him'; 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'; and 8 more.

Only in Praise of Hapi who comes forth to make Egypt live (Nile Hymn, pSallier II, 11,6-12,9): The flood god creates barley and emmer so that the temples may feast; when offerings to the gods fail, men perish; The flood god is greeted as king, constant in his laws, coming forth before Upper and Lower Egypt; The flood is fashioned by the potter god Khnum; When the flood rises the land is in jubilation: every belly rejoices, every jaw laughs, every tooth is bared; Foreign highlands far from the river are watered by the water that comes down from the sky (rain); The Nile-flood god (Hapi) comes forth from the earth to make Egypt live; If the flood god is sluggish, the multitudes are impoverished, the gods' offerings dwindle and millions of people perish; A god whose form is hidden, whose place is unknown, whose cavern is not found in the writings and whose name is not known even in the underworld; The god brings the river flood and abundance, makes plenty sprout in seas and reed-beds, and creates grain, the life of the people.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The lover goes down to his garden or nut orchard to graze, gather lilies and see if the vines have blossomed (weight 7.3); Love poetry in alternating voices of a woman, her lover and a chorus (daughters of Jerusalem) (weight 6.2). Pair score 13.6.

Only in Love lyrics of Nabû and Tašmetu (SAA 3 14): The beloved's body is praised part by part in similes (thighs a gazelle, ankles an apple, heels obsidian); The lover wishes his eyes to see the plucking of her fruit and his ears to hear her birds' song (garden imagery for love); The lovers' meeting place is the shade of cedar, cypress and juniper; The divine wedding of Nabû and Tašmetu is celebrated with the goddess taken to the cella and bed; Confession of trust: 'let whoever trusts, trust (in his own); we trust in our god'; Formula on trust: let whoever trusts, trust; we trust in our god / on God let the trusters trust; The god's consort enters her bedchamber in the new temple and rests with him on the bed.

Only in Where has your beloved gone; the beloved unique among queens: The beloved is unique ('one is my dove') among sixty queens, eighty concubines and countless maidens, who praise her; The beloved looks forth like the dawn, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, awesome as bannered hosts; Her hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead; Her teeth are like a flock of shorn ewes come up from washing, all bearing twins, none bereaved; Chorus: 'What is your beloved more than another beloved, O fairest of women?'; Her lips like a scarlet thread, her cheek (raqqah) like a slice of pomegranate behind her veil; Mutual-belonging formula: 'My beloved is mine and I am his'; Wasf: a descriptive song praising the beloved's body part by part with images from nature and architecture.

Only in Three vassals under one oath; disputes before the king (CTH 67 §§8-11): A dispute between fellow vassals is not to be pursued by rash hostility but brought before the great king, who judges it and sets them back on the road; Fellow vassals bound by one oath must be of one mind: not harm, kill or seize one another, not shelter one another's runaways, and fight a common enemy together; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself.

Only in Underworld Vision: before Nergal's throne; Išum intercedes; the prince is sent back (SAA 3 32 rev. 11-21): A divine adviser (Išum) intercedes with the angry god who wants to kill the seer: 'Do not let the young man die'; The angry god's voice roars over the seer like a raging storm; The netherworld king (Nergal) sits on a royal throne with a crown, holding two fierce maces, lightning flashing from his arms, the Anunnaki kneeling right and left; Overwhelmed by the god's radiance, the seer trembles, kisses the god's feet and kneels; The seer is seized by the forelock (abūsātu) and dragged before the enthroned god; The vision seizes the prophet with labor pains; he is bowed down, terrified and his twilight pleasure turns to trembling; The god releases the visionary from the netherworld with a commission: may this word lodge like a thorn in your heart, go up and proclaim it; A man is seized by the forelock and brought before the judging deity [divergence between the texts]; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

Only in Vision of abominations in the temple - image of jealousy, animal chamber, Tammuz, sun worship: Idolaters 'put the branch (zemorah) to their nose', an obscure cultic gesture; Seventy elders stand with censers in hand offering incense in the dark, each in his chamber of images; A human-like figure of fire from the waist down and gleaming like hashmal (amber/electrum) from the waist up; Though they cry in God's ears with a loud voice, he will not listen; An idol called 'the image (semel) of jealousy that provokes jealousy' stands at the north gate of the temple; Prophet is told to dig through a wall and enters through the opening; Hidden temple chamber whose walls are engraved all around with creeping things, loathsome beasts and idols; God carried his servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque; About twenty-five men with their backs to the temple bow eastward to the sun between the porch and the altar; Prophet in exile is brought 'in visions of God' to the Jerusalem temple; Elders of the people come and sit before the prophet in his house to inquire; The glory of YHWH appears in the cloud; and 5 more.

Only in The Sin of Sargon: Sennacherib divines why his father died unburied (SAA 3 33): A king investigates by divination the sin for which his father died a bad death; The diviners, divided into separate groups so they cannot confer, give the same answer 'with one mouth'; The king ponders daily in his heart: who can understand the works of the gods?; Court scribes prevent the king from making the statue of a god, and his life is cut short; The king's father sinned by honouring the gods of Assyria above the gods of Babylon and not keeping the treaty of the king of the gods; The fallen king is cast out of his grave like a loathed branch, unburied among the slain, while other kings lie in honor; Swear only by God's name; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

Only in David's charge to Solomon, death and burial: The dying king instructs his successor to execute old enemies; The king 'slept with his fathers' and was buried in the City of David; A man is granted to eat at the king's table continually; Refrain: the kingdom was established in the king's hand; Father says losing his son will bring his grey hairs down to Sheol in sorrow; A king's age at accession and length of reign are given; Death called 'going the way of all the earth'; The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness.

Only in The Marduk Ordeal: Bēl held captive, sought by the goddess, the criminal killed with him (SAA 3 34, obv. 1-33): A criminal (bēl hiṭṭi) is held with the captive god and killed; his head is tied to the goddess's chariot; Milk is drawn before Ištar of Nineveh because she raised the god and showed him mercy; An ecstatic (mahhû) goes before the goddess weeping as messenger, crying 'my brother, my brother!'; The god, shut in by the gods in the temple tower (or tomb), escapes and is brought down from it; The chief god (Bēl/Marduk) is held captive in the 'mountain' or prison house, guarded, and later comes out; The son god (Nabû) comes from his city to ask after the welfare of his captive father; The captive god's consort stretches out her hands and prays to Sîn and Šamaš: 'let Bēl live!'; A goddess roams the streets searching for the captive god: 'where is he held?' and goes to the gate of the grave; A cultic commentary explains each ritual act or object of a festival as an episode of a myth ('the X which ... is the Y').

Only in KTU 1.12 II: Baal approaches the Devourers and seizes them, or is seized; he falls like a bull in the marsh, clothed in his brothers' blood; for seven years, eight cycles, El lets the fields wither; the king ceases to judge, the water-drawers leave the spring, the noise in El's house ceases: At the god's fall the king ceases to judge, the women drawing water leave the spring, the noise in El's house and the clatter of the craftsman's house cease; A god lies clothed in the blood of his brothers as in a garment, of his kin as in a cloak; At a disaster the ordinary sounds cease: water-drawers at the spring, the noise of the house, the clatter of the workshop; The storm god falls like a bull, sinks like an ox in the marsh, clothed in the blood of his brothers; Seven years El fills, eight cycles of time, while the produce of the fields is scorched; In the ruined city the seat of judgment stands empty and no decisions or justice are given; Seven years of drought or hardship in which the land yields nothing; The storm god takes his bow in his hand and arrows in his right and goes to the marsh full of wild bulls.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Wisdom was brought forth (holalti, 'born in travail') when there were no deeps or springs, before mountains were sunk and hills existed (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in The Marduk Ordeal: Enūma eliš recited, Aššur before heaven and earth, Anzû defeated, the god freed; curse (SAA 3 34, obv. 34-76): A goddess as wailing woman (bākītu) goes round the city lamenting; Enūma eliš is reinterpreted: before heaven and earth were created, Aššur existed; The god's chariot goes to the festival house without its lord, rocking empty; The creation epic Enūma eliš is recited (sung) before the god in the month Nisan; The chief god (Bēl/Marduk) is held captive in the 'mountain' or prison house, guarded, and later comes out; Colophon curse: whoever erases or soaks this tablet, or shows it to one who is not initiated, may the gods curse him; The captive god prays to the sun god: 'I did good deeds for (the high god); what is my sin?' and begs to be kept alive; Curse: may the gods eradicate his name and seed from the land and give his flesh to the mouth of dogs; Those of the dynasty who die in the city are eaten by dogs, those in the field by birds; The news of the champion's victory reaches the gods' temple and the high god and his wife rejoice; The warrior god (Ninurta, or Nabû in commentary) defeats and kills the Anzu bird.

Only in Proverbs 8:22-31, Wisdom before and at creation: 'YHWH acquired (or created, qanani) me as the beginning (reshit) of his way, the first of his works of old'; Wisdom was beside God as an 'amon' (master craftsman, or nursling/child); Wisdom's delight was with the sons of man (benei adam); Wisdom was 'installed' or 'woven' (nissakhti) from eternity, from the beginning, before the earth; Wisdom was God's delight day by day, playing (mesaheqet) before him always, playing in his inhabited world; Wisdom was present when God established the heavens, drew the circle on the deep, fixed the clouds, set the sea's limit and marked earth's foundations; God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; Earth built like a structure with measurements, measuring line, sunk bases and a cornerstone; God sets a boundary the sea may not pass, so it will never again cover the earth; God made all his works in wisdom; Before creation there is a dark watery deep (tehom) out of which the world is formed; Before creation there was no rain, plant or man to till the ground (when-not-yet opening); and 3 more.

Only in Shipwrecked Sailor: the promised offerings; the serpent laughs - 'I am the ruler of Punt'; the ship comes: The rescued man promises to report his saviour's might to the king and to send incense, oils, burnt offerings and laden ships as to a god; The divine being laughs at the mortal's promise of offerings: 'I am the ruler of Punt; the myrrh is mine'; Once the visitor leaves, the enchanted island will never be seen again, for it will become water; The divine helper's only request: 'Make my good name known in your city'; The deity declines the mortal's gifts of food or offerings [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; The divine being foretells the exact time of rescue: after four months a ship with sailors the castaway knows will come and take him home.

Only in Josiah's covenant, purge of the cults and Passover; death at Megiddo: Idolatrous cult objects are burned and their dust carried away or thrown on graves; Despite the righteous king's reform, God does not turn from his anger over a predecessor's sins; Horses dedicated to the sun at the temple entrance and chariots of the sun burned; The high places Solomon built on the 'mount of destruction' (Mount of Olives) for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom; The righteous king is killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Necho; Priests of the high places are slaughtered on their own altars; The bones of a prophet are left undisturbed when other graves are desecrated; Priests of the high places may not serve at the altar but eat unleavened bread among their brothers; The Tophet in the valley of Ben-hinnom is defiled so no one may burn children to Molech; A Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges; Women weave 'houses' (garments, hangings) for Asherah in the temple precinct; A covenant is made between God, the king and the people; and 11 more.

Only in The sick king's plea through the Sun to his god (CTH 374 §22-44): Through illness the sufferer's house has become a house of fear and his soul drifts elsewhere; The merchant who falsifies the scales before the sun god is contrasted with the sufferer who has done nothing to his god; The sufferer says he drifts like a boat on the river and does not know his destination; The sufferer asks whether his god wrote his illness down for him from his mother's womb; At night in his bed no pleasant dream comes to the sufferer and his name does not appear for good; The petitioner asks the sun god, who reaches heaven and earth, to go to the angry god wherever he is and deliver the man's words; Address to the personal god: 'You are my father who begot me; lift up my face'; In adversity the god takes the sufferer's hand, slaps him awake with the right hand and raises his head with the left.

Only in Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 14-19: the friend reproves; the sufferer on social inversion; wealth and poverty ordained: Long life is the god's to grant; wealth and poverty were fixed by the gods since days of old; A suffering man and his learned friend debate in alternating speeches why the pious suffer while the impious prosper; A creature digs a pit into which the proud hero falls and cannot climb out; The great gods fashion the black-headed people and make the animals multiply; The poem is an alphabetic acrostic (lines or stanzas begin with successive letters).

Only in The land in sickness - civil war, social reversal, the sun withdrawn (Neferti 38/3-57/2): In the age of chaos men make weapons of copper and demand bread with blood; No one weeps for the dead or fasts at night for them, mourning customs lapse, because every heart is concerned only with itself; The land is diminished but its rulers are many; it is empty but its taxes are great; grain is scarce but the measure is large; A man's possessions are taken from him and given to an outsider; the owner grieves while the stranger is content; The holy city, birthplace of every god (Heliopolis), no longer exists for the land; The sun god separates himself from humankind: his hour cannot be known, his shadow is not seen, he is in the sky only like the moon; Refrain of the seer: 'I show you the land in sickness' (or 'I show you the son as foe...'), introducing each list of woes; Son dishonors father, daughter rises against mother, daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; a man's enemies are his own household; A man flees from his brother, each concerned only with himself.

sides.note: Bata as a bull to his wife: 'See, I am still alive.' 'Who are you?' 'I am Bata. I know that when you had the cedar felled it was to keep me from living' (15_8/2-15_10). evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 21.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 5 more.

Only in Slander, the great kings, Ahhiyawa erased, embargo on Assyria (CTH 105 §§10-14): The king of Ahhiyawa is written among the great kings of equal rank and then erased from the tablet; The vassal's merchants may not go to the enemy land (Assyria), nor may its merchants enter or cross the vassal's land; one who comes is to be seized and sent to the king; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 15.9.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 6 more.

Only in Protect the king's line; do not act like Mašturi; be ready to die (CTH 105 §§5-9): A vassal betrays his benefactor's son, asking 'shall I protect a bastard?', and is held up in a later treaty as a warning; The great king takes the vassal by the hand, gives him his sister in marriage, makes him his brother-in-law and king of his land; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions (weight 6.0); The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 16.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Arnuwanda's oath for the men of Išmerika: witnesses and curses (CTH 133 §§1-4): Treaty curse: may the gods destroy the oath-breaker's name and seed from the earth; An oath sworn by the life of Heaven and the life of Earth.

Pair score 15.4.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 6 more.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 27.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 4 more.

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed.

Only in Šunaššura treaty, Hittite version (CTH 41.II.1): defectors, fugitives, the penalty of twelve persons: Whoever hides a fugitive in his house must give twelve persons in compensation, or himself be killed; a hiding slave's master may forfeit him; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same').

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 34.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting; and 3 more.

Only in Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §9-26: oath gods destroy the oath-breaker, blessing for the loyal, enemy of the king, no excuse of neutrality: Treaty curse: 'these oath gods shall not leave you in peace, shall not release you, shall destroy you' (and whoever you side with); The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Blessing and curse set before the people as a choice.
