evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people (weight 5.7); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 16.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in Ḫuqqana treaty (CTH 42) §7-8: the list of divine witnesses, mountains, rivers, springs, clouds, heaven, earth and the great sea: The treaty is sworn before a list of gods (including the vassal's own gods) or before the planets and stars, who guarantee it.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land (weight 6.0); Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions (weight 6.0); Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people (weight 5.7); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 28.6.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting; and 4 more.

Only in CTH 51.I §17-18: the gods of Mittani incl. Mitra, Varuna, Indra; curses on the oath-breaker; blessings for the loyal: Treaty blessing: may your sons and grandsons rule as kings for ever and your father's throne grow old; Treaty curse: may the oath crush you with your land like a reed; Treaty curse: may the ground be ice so that you slip, and your land a pond in which you sink; Treaty curse: may the oath gods give you poverty and nakedness; Treaty curse: you shall be enemies of the thousand gods and they shall hunt you down; Mitra, Varuna, Indra and the Nāsatyas are invoked as witnesses of a Mittani treaty; Treaty blessing: may the land be restored as of old, grow rich and lie down (rabāṣu) in peace; Simile curse: as malt in the mash does not sprout, may your seed vanish from the land; Treaty curse: may the gods overturn your throne; Blessing and curse set before the people as a choice; Treaty curse: may the gods destroy the oath-breaker's name and seed from the earth.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in CTH 51.I §9-15: stipulations - the treaty, aid, fugitives returned one way only, the Euphrat border, brotherhood of Piyaššili and Šattiwazza: Escaped slave not returned to his master; he may live where he chooses; Each party swears not to cross the boundary (a river, a heap) into the other's side; The great king says he will bring a dead (ruined) land back to life and restore it to its place; A dead (ruined) land or town is brought back to life [divergence between the texts]; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; A fugitive who comes over is not handed back, because returning him is not right under the divine rule; The overlord fixes and seals the vassal's borders for him and his descendants for ever, listing the frontier towns and mountains one by one; The treaty tablet ends: whoever changes this treaty, may the named gods (storm god, sun god, city goddesses) be the lords of his oath (avenge it).

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in CTH 52.I §11-12: the gods of Mittani; Šattiwazza and the Hurrians curse themselves - tamarisk, water of the gutter, smoke, salt; their blessing in the lord's shade: Self-curse: as salt has no seed, so may we have no seed; like a dissolved lump of salt may we not be restored; Self-curse: as a felled tree (tamarisk/acacia) puts out no shoot, so may we have no seed; Self-curse: may we rise like smoke to heaven; The vassal asks that the great king love him and his land as he loves his own lands, sons and his own tablet; The sworn people pray to eat a rich harvest in their lord's shade (ṣillu) while he goes before them; The sworn speak in the first person ('if we ...') and call on the named gods to seek out their seed if they rebel; Mitra, Varuna, Indra and the Nāsatyas are invoked as witnesses of a Mittani treaty; Mortality likened to water spilled on the ground that cannot be gathered up; Treaty blessing: may the land be restored as of old, grow rich and lie down (rabāṣu) in peace; Treaty curse: may the gods overturn your throne; The vassal may keep concubines but may take no wife above or equal to the overlord's sister or daughter, who must be chief wife; The people and lands relax under the king's broad protection (an-dul3, 'shade').

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; and 6 more.

Only in Mountains, rivers, heaven and earth as witnesses; curse and blessing (CTH 53 §§21-22): An oath sworn by the life of Heaven and the life of Earth; A text ends with a note on its source or on where it was written.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Tribute, audience, friend and enemy, wholehearted war (CTH 53 §§5-7): The vassal must go up every year to the overlord's land to appear before his lord; The vassal's yearly tribute in refined first-class gold is fixed and is to be weighed by the weights of the overlord's merchants; If the vassal writes to the enemy 'the troops of Hatti are coming to attack you; be on your guard', he has broken the oath; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); Forbidden: sending secret messages to the overlord's (God's) enemy; Warriors come 'with a whole heart', 'not with a double heart', with one heart to make the king; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath (weight 7.3); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 29.0.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; and 4 more.

Only in Aid in revolt, feeding troops, captives, evil words and secret orders (CTH 62 §§12-16): If the king secretly orders something that cannot be done, the vassal must protest on the spot 'I cannot do this and I will not do it'; failing to do a feasible order breaks the oath; A secret word confided by the ruler must be kept; divulging it is a breach; When the overlord's troops march into the vassal's towns he must give them food and drink; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods (weight 6.8); Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 17.8.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in The witness gods of Hatti and Amurru (CTH 62 §§21-24): Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; A mountain is written with the divine determinative and receives cult as a god; The storm god of Mount Hazzi (Ṣapon, Jebel Aqra) is invoked as a witness god; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5). Pair score 17.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Egypt, secret envoys, the half-hearted ally (CTH 62 §§8-11): The vassal must not secretly send his messenger to a rival great king (Egypt) nor push away the overlord's hand and become that king's vassal; If the vassal writes to the enemy 'the troops of Hatti are coming to attack you; be on your guard', he has broken the oath; Forbidden: sending secret messages to the overlord's (God's) enemy.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in Calling for troops, runaway soldiers, Arzawa captives (CTH 67 §§12-14): The vassal must look after the overlord's garrison troops as after his own person and house, support them and do them no harm.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0). Pair score 10.4.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in Manapa-Tarḫunta's flight, the oath gods seize the rebels, his plea for life (CTH 69 §§1-4): While still a child the heir is threatened by his brothers, who try to kill him; he escapes to a foreign people, who shelter him at the great king's word; A rebel vassal falls at the great king's feet and writes 'My lord, let me live, do not destroy me, take me as your servant, protect my person', and is pardoned; While still a child, the favoured son is threatened with death by his brothers and ends up in a foreign land; A treaty's historical prologue recounts how the great king rescued, restored or spared the vassal (or his ancestor), making that past benefit the ground of the vassal's obligation; A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land (weight 6.0); Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions (weight 6.0); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 17.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 6 more.

Only in Destroyed from the dark earth, or protected (CTH 69 §§26-28): Treaty blessing: the loyal vassal shall see good prosperity and grow old in the hand of the great king; The treaty tablet ends: whoever changes this treaty, may the named gods (storm god, sun god, city goddesses) be the lords of his oath (avenge it); A text ends with a note on its source or on where it was written.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); Fugitives who flee from one realm to the other must be handed back (weight 5.0); The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it (weight 4.9). Pair score 16.2.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in Mankind is corrupt; the four kings of Arzawa; borders; fugitives (CTH 76 §§15-18): 'Because mankind is unreliable, rumours go round': if someone whispers that the king plans evil against the vassal, he must write to the king and wait, not act rashly; A free fugitive from the vassal's land who reaches Hatti is not returned ('it is not right'), but a farmer or craftsman who fled without doing his work is seized and sent back; Fellow vassals bound by one oath must be of one mind: not harm, kill or seize one another, not shelter one another's runaways, and fight a common enemy together; A rumour or report must be checked before anyone acts on it: referred to the ruler, or verified; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath (weight 5.8); The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting (weight 5.5); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 16.5.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 6 more.

Only in The witness gods, with the gods of Wiluša and Appaliuna (CTH 76 §§20-23): A god [A]ppaliuna (possibly Apollo) is named among the gods of Wiluša (perhaps Troy) invoked as treaty witnesses; The underground watercourses (KASKAL.KUR, sinkholes) of a land are invoked among the treaty witnesses; Among the treaty witnesses the moon god is called 'lord of the oath' and Išḫara 'queen of the oath'; The storm god of Mount Hazzi (Ṣapon, Jebel Aqra) is invoked as a witness god; The gods of the lulaḫḫi mountain-folk and the gods of the Habiru (ḫapiri) are named among the treaty witnesses; The primeval 'gods of eternity' (Nara, Namšara, Minki, Ammunki, Alalu, Anu, Antu, Enlil, Ninlil) are invoked as treaty witnesses; The sun god is shepherd of the land and father of the black-headed.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; and 7 more.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; and 7 more.

Only in Alakšandu's chosen son, mutual protection, the fugitive conspirator (CTH 76 §§6-9): If the vassal's brother or kin rebels and seeks the throne, the overlord will recognise only the vassal, not accept the rebel, and destroy the rebel's land; The overlord promises that the son the vassal will beget shall be king after him and shall be protected as his father is; The treaty tablet, sealed with the god's own seal, is set before the sworn, who must guard it like their god and not alter, erase, burn, drown or bury it; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know' (weight 6.4); The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy (weight 6.0); When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help (weight 5.9); The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly (weight 5.6); The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy (weight 5.5). Pair score 29.3.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people; The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself; The 'thousand gods' (līm ilānī) of Hatti are summoned to assemble and hear the oath, or invoked in a greeting; and 4 more.

Only in Friend and enemy, half-hearted war, mutual aid (CTH 92 §§10-16): If the vassal writes to the enemy 'the troops of Hatti are coming to attack you; be on your guard', he has broken the oath; The great king lists the kings of equal rank to himself: the kings of Egypt, Babylonia, Hanigalbat or Assyria (and Ahhiyawa); A ruler who did not keep the treaty sworn by the gods is punished by them (defeat, death, abandonment).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The vassal must not set another king or another lord over himself (weight 5.7); The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come (weight 5.3). Pair score 11.0.

Only in Treaty of Muršili II of Hatti with Niqmepa of Ugarit: loyalty, mutual help, fugitives, secrecy; the thousand gods as witnesses; curse and blessing (RS 17.0079+): The overlord seats the vassal on his father's throne and returns to him the land of his father, making him his servant; A covenant is framed so that the bound party cannot later say 'I did not know'; The sovereign party of a bond requires the other to treat 'my enemy' as an enemy, not as a friend; Whether people who flee from the other side of a treaty are handed back [contrast between the texts]; Words the overlord tells the vassal in secret must be kept secret; revealing them breaks the oath; The male and female gods of the vassal land (Ugarit) are named as witnesses alongside the overlord's own gods; The vassal may not excuse inaction by saying 'I am bound by oath and treaty; whether the enemy kills them or they kill him, I do not know'; Treaty blessing: if the vassal keeps the words written on the tablet, the oath gods guard him with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city and land; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath; and 7 more.

Only in I was a dead man, you brought me back to life: Bentešina asks for a sealed tablet (CTH 92 §§6-9): Curse: the oath gods shall kill the oath-breaker and burn him; As the vassal's own soul, body, wife, children and land are precious to him, so the king's soul and person, wife, children and land must be precious to him; A living man is called a dead man whom his benefactor has brought back to life; The overlord promises the vassal that, once victorious, he will give him a sealed tablet of treaty; The restored vassal is described, or describes himself, as a dead man whom the great king brought back to life; The ruler (crown prince, prophet) is to be loved as, or to be closer than, one's own self [divergence between the texts]; The sworn must not set one of the designated heir's brothers, elder or younger, on the throne in his place; A treaty is rewritten after the wording of the tablet the great king's grandfather gave to the vassal's ancestor, which the intervening kings had held to.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The overlord grants the vassal that whatever troops or fugitives of the rebel neighbouring lands he captures no one may take from his hand (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Šuppiluliuma I to Niqmaddu of Ugarit: do not fear Nuhašše and Mukiš; keep the treaty, and the booty and fugitives you take are yours (RS 17.0132): The overlord promises the vassal that, once victorious, he will give him a sealed tablet of treaty; The overlord tells the vassal 'do not fear' the hostile neighbouring kings and promises to deal with them; The overlord points the vassal to neighbouring kings who abandoned the treaty: 'later you will see what the great king does to them'; The vassal serves the king as his father and his father's father served him; The vassal must love the king and his friends and hate his enemy; A letter opens with the formula 'Say to my lord (X): thus says Y, your servant' (or, from the king, 'thus says your lord').

Only in Šunaššura treaty CTH 41.I.2 §11-47: mutual protection, enemies, booty, aid, reporting, envoys: A king's son, servant or envoy sent to the other king must suffer no harm and must not be caught with magic herbs; 'How good and pleasant when brothers dwell together in unity'; The vassal must love the overlord's head, soul and body as he loves his own and keep his hands around him; Each king will protect in the kingship the son whom the other designates as heir; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Those who incite rebellion must be seized, put in fetters and delivered to the king, or killed; The overlord promises that if anyone presses the vassal, he himself, a prince or a great lord will come with troops and chariots and kill the enemy; When an enemy rises or a revolt breaks out against the overlord, the vassal must go at once with his troops and chariots (or send his son or brother) to help; The vassal must take up the bow, stand with the king and fight his enemy wholeheartedly; The oath binds not only those present but their sons and grandsons and all who will exist in days to come; The sworn party must report any seditious or evil word heard against the king, whether from a brother, the king's own seed, an official, a friend or anyone, and must not conceal it.

passages.text: (§21:181) [ … -]el tup-pí-aš INIM{MEŠ} wa-aḫ-nu-š[i] (§21:182) [ … ] Nach der Textzusammenstellung von Kühne – Otten 1971, 80 ist B Vs. 8-9 folgendermaßen zu lesen: (8) [ ca. 16-17 Zeichen AŠ-ŠU]M EN-UT-TIM [ _ (_) -t]a nu IT-TI ⌈KUR⌉ [{U]RU}⌈Ḫa⌉-at-ti-[a _ _ -]x (9) [ ca. 12-13 Zeichen KUR {URU}Ḫa-at-t]i-a pa-aḫ-ḫa[- _ _ ] wa-aš-ta-aš. Der Schreiber in Exemplar B scheint die beiden Sätze B Vs. 8 [ … AŠ-Š]UM EN-UT-TIM [PAP-aš-t]a und B Vs. 9 [ … KUR {URU}Ḫa-at-t]i-a pa-aḫ-ḫa-a[š-ta] direkt untereinander gesetzt zu haben. Nach der Textedition steht waštaš (Vs. 9) ohne eine Satzeinleitung nach paḫḫa[šta], obwohl ein freier Raum zwischen den beiden Worten vorhanden ist. Mit Kühne – Otten 1971, 31 ist deshalb wahrscheinlich nu ITTI KUR {URU}Ḫatti=a (B Vs. 8) waštaš (B Vs. 9) zu nu ITTI ⌈KUR {URU}Ḫatti=a⌉ [Ú-UL ku-it-k]i waštaš zusammenzufassen. Diesen Satz hat der Schreiber zuerst (wahrscheinlich) vergessen und erst später eingefügt. Weil der linke Rand bereits durch das Ende von B Vs. 7 beansprucht war, standen dem Schreiber nur die - bis dahin leeren - Zeilenenden von B Vs. 8-9 für diesen Zusatz zur Verfügung. Da der vorhandene Raum B Vs. 8-9 nicht ausreicht, um den Text A I 22-25 aufzunehmen, dürfte B eine Variante – nach Kühne – Otten 1971, 31 (I 22 f.) die einzige nachweisbare Textvariante – enthalten. Vermutlich hat der Schreiber entweder den Text von A I 22-23 oder den Text A I 24-25 (versehentlich?) weggelassen. Das Exemplar B ist somit wahrscheinlich als Abschrift zu betrachten.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Heaven and earth called as witnesses against the people (weight 5.7); A long roster of the great gods and the gods of each city and land is named as present at the conclusion of the treaty (weight 5.2). Pair score 10.8.

Only in Šauška-muwa of Amurru swears not to do murder against ʿAmmistamru of Ugarit, his ships or troops, over the daughter of the Great Lady; heaven and earth and the gods to know (RS 17.0365+): A king divorces (or harms) his royal wife, 'the daughter of the Great Lady' (a Hittite or Amurrite princess), and the case is decided by the great kings; A king swears not to do murder (nērtu) against a neighbouring king, his ships or his troops; if he does, the gods are to destroy him from his father's house, land and throne; Treaty curse: the oath gods are to destroy the oath-breaker together with his person, wives, sons, grandsons, house, city, land and all his possessions.

Only in Treaty of Tutḫaliya I with Šunaššura, Akkadian version KBo 28.110 (CTH 41.I.1): the ox and its stall, the tablet, the gods: The vassal is to trust a messenger only if his spoken words agree with the words written on the tablet he brings; A rival is condemned by his own earlier answer ('Just so!') to the very case now turned against him; The tablet of a vassal's former oath to a rival overlord is erased, the rival's word rejected and a new tablet made; The great king releases a land from a former overlord's oath, an act of 'release' (andurāru); When the vassal comes before the great king he may see the king's face and no grandee sits above him; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); Treaty curse: may the gods destroy the oath-breaker's name and seed from the earth; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath.

Only in Treaty of Tutḫaliya I with Šunaššura, Akkadian version KBo 28.110 (CTH 41.I.1): the ox and its stall, the tablet, the gods: The vassal is to trust a messenger only if his spoken words agree with the words written on the tablet he brings; A rival is condemned by his own earlier answer ('Just so!') to the very case now turned against him; The tablet of a vassal's former oath to a rival overlord is erased, the rival's word rejected and a new tablet made; The great king releases a land from a former overlord's oath, an act of 'release' (andurāru); When the vassal comes before the great king he may see the king's face and no grandee sits above him; Ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know (animals wiser than God's people); Treaty curse: may the gods destroy the oath-breaker's name and seed from the earth; A parity treaty repeats each obligation with the roles of the two kings exchanged ('and for the other the same'); Mountains, rivers, springs, the great sea, heaven and earth, winds and clouds are named among the witnesses of a treaty or oath.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A woman accused of harlotry is sentenced to be burned (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Westcar: Khafre's tale: Ubaoner's wife and the commoner; the wax crocodile; the adulteress burned: The magician commands the crocodile to bring up the man from the depths and later the king tells it to take away 'what is yours'; no one knows where it took him; A priest's wife takes a commoner as lover; they spend the day drinking in the pavilion of his garden lake and the caretaker reports it to the husband; A magician makes a crocodile of wax; thrown into the water after the adulterer it becomes a real crocodile of seven cubits and seizes him; picked up again it is wax; Portrait of the man who slept with another man's wife: no one walks with him, life passes him by, no just man holds him dear, he is thrown away like a worthless coin and clothed as if under heavy punishment; An object thrown down becomes a live beast and, taken in the hand, returns to what it was [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; After each wonder tale the king orders offerings (a thousand loaves, a hundred jars of beer, an ox, incense) for the dead king and his magician: 'I have seen his deed of knowledge'; Adulterer and adulteress both put to death; The king's sons rise one after another to tell the king a wonder (bjꜣ,yt) worked by a magician-priest in the days of a former king.

Only in Judah and Tamar: Man spills his seed on the ground to avoid raising offspring for his dead brother and is struck dead; God kills a man for unspecified wickedness; A kid of the goats promised as a harlot's hire; Seal, cord and staff left as a pledge, later used as proof of paternity; Midwife ties a scarlet thread on the hand of the twin who emerges first; Man acknowledges the wronged woman: 'She is more righteous than I'; Twins contend at birth over who emerges first; A widow veils herself, sits by the road and is taken for a harlot by her father-in-law; Father-in-law withholds his youngest son from the widow, fearing he too will die; Evidence presented with the formula 'Please recognize (haker na)' whose is this; What a woman's veil or cloak signals to men who see her [contrast between the texts]; Sheep-shearing as an occasion for travel and festivity; and 2 more.

sides.note: As in 2Chr 9:8: the Kings queen blesses 'YHWH your God' for loving Israel and setting Solomon on the throne of Israel; the Quran's queen submits with Solomon to the Lord of the worlds. A foreigner's praise of Israel's God becomes a conversion to the universal Lord.

passages.text: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֗ לְתִתְּךָ֤ עַל כִּסְאוֹ֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת אֱלֹהֶ֤יךָ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְהַעֲמִיד֣וֹ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּתֶּנְךָ֤ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָֽה

sides.note: The queen's last word: Chronicles has a blessing of Solomon's God, yəhî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkā bārûkh ʾăšer ḥāfēṣ bəkhā lə-tittəkhā ʿal kisʾô, 'your God', praised for Israel's king. The Quran has a conversion: rabbi innī ẓalamtu nafsī wa-aslamtu maʿa Sulaymāna lillāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn, after the hoopoe reported that she and her people worshipped the sun (27:24). Chronicles never calls her an idolater.

leads.title: Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit ↔ Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death
leads.summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A false prophet strikes the true prophet on the cheek (weight 7.7); Court prophet makes iron horns: 'with these you will gore Aram' (weight 7.7); Four hundred court prophets unanimously promise victory (weight 7.7); Prophet first sarcastically repeats the favorable oracle, then under oath tells the true one (weight 7.7); A single true prophet, hated by the king because he never prophesies good for him (weight 7.7); A spirit volunteers in the divine council to be a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths (weight 7.3); Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd' (weight 6.5). Pair score 52.6.

Only in Micaiah son of Imlah and the lying spirit: Prophet imprisoned on short rations of bread and water until the king returns in peace; God asks the heavenly council 'who will entice the king?'; a spirit volunteers; Prophet stakes his authority: 'If you return in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me'; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [divergence between the texts]; Prophet sees God seated on his throne with all the host of heaven standing to his right and left; Whether the adversary, devils or deceiving spirits have access to God's council [contrast between the texts]; God uses a false prophet to test whether Israel loves him.

Only in Micaiah ben Imlah, the lying spirit in the divine council, and Ahab's death: The enemy commander orders his chariots to fight no one but the king; When the threatened king cries out, God turns the attackers away from him; 'Hear, all you peoples' (quotation linking the prophet to Micah); One king entices (hesit) another into a disastrous war; Two kings sit in royal robes on thrones at the threshing floor by the city gate; A righteous king allies by marriage with a wicked king's house; Prophet imprisoned on 'bread of affliction and water of affliction'; The prophet swears to speak only what his God tells him; The wounded king props himself in his chariot all day and dies at sunset; An arrow shot at random strikes the king between the joints of his armor; A king disguises himself in battle while his ally wears royal robes; God enthroned with the host of heaven standing at his right and left deliberates.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Bronze vessels cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zarethan (weight 7.7); The bronze used for the sanctuary is so abundant its weight was not determined (weight 7.7); A round vessel ten cubits across measures thirty around (pi taken as three) (weight 7.7); An accounting of the gold, silver and bronze used for the sanctuary (weight 7.1); A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God (weight 6.8); A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes (weight 6.8). Pair score 43.9.

Only in The bronze sea, wheeled stands and temple vessels: Ten golden lampstands stand before the inner sanctuary, five on each side; Ten wheeled bronze stands decorated with lions, oxen, cherubim and palms carry basins; How Solomon's great bronze works were produced [divergence between the texts]; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; A small gold-plated altar for burning incense before the veil; A bronze laver where priests wash hands and feet before service, lest they die.

Only in Bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, lavers, lampstands and tables: A great bronze altar twenty cubits square and ten high; The temple has a court of the priests and a great court; The rim of the bronze sea is shaped like a lily blossom; The bronze sea serves for the priests to wash in, the lavers for rinsing offerings; Ten gold lampstands and ten tables, five on each side; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A foreigner from a far land who hears of God's name comes to pray at the temple and is heard (weight 7.7); 'There is no man who does not sin' (weight 7.7); Heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain God, much less a temple (weight 7.1); The direction faced in prayer [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Prayers made toward the temple (or toward the land, city and house when in exile) are heard in heaven (weight 7.1); Prophet spreads out his palms to God in prayer (weight 6.5); Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to God (weight 6.5). Pair score 49.6.

Only in Solomon's prayer of dedication: Exiles in an enemy land turn back with all their heart and pray toward their land, and God grants them mercy before captors; A man accused swears a curse-oath before the altar, and God judges guilty and innocent; Egypt called an iron furnace (smelting furnace); Heaven is shut and no rain falls because of the people's sin; repentance brings rain; Long catalogue of curses for covenant violation (disease, defeat, famine, exile); God alone knows the hearts of all humans.

Only in Solomon's blessing and dedication prayer on the bronze platform: The king kneels on a bronze platform in the court and spreads his hands to heaven; People away from Jerusalem or in exile pray in the direction of the land, city and temple; Captives confess in exile 'We have sinned, done wrong and acted wickedly'; 'Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and the ark of your might'; Prayer lists famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, siege and sickness as occasions for prayer; An oath sworn before God's altar in the temple, judged by God; Temple called a 'house of zebul' (exalted dwelling), a place for God to dwell forever; 'O my servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy; God forgives all sins'; God has said he will dwell in thick darkness ('arafel); The dynasty's continuance is conditioned on the heirs' faithfulness; God looks on the heart, not on appearance or height; Sacrifice only at the place God will choose to make his name dwell; and 1 more.

בְּהֵעָצֵ֥ר שָׁמַ֛יִם וְלֹא יִהְיֶ֥ה מָטָ֖ר כִּ֣י יֶחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֞וּ אֶל הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ וְהוֹד֣וּ אֶת שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וּמֵחַטָּאתָ֥ם יְשׁוּב֖וּן כִּ֥י תַעֲנֵֽם
כִּי יֵצֵ֨א עַמְּךָ֤ לַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עַל אֹ֣יְב֔וֹ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁלָחֵ֑ם וְהִתְפַּֽלְל֣וּ אֶל יְהוָ֗ה דֶּ֤רֶךְ הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתָּ בָּ֔הּ וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥תִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ

לִהְיוֹת֩ עֵינֶ֨יךָ פְתֻח֜וֹת אֶל הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אֶל הַ֨מָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתָּ לָשׂ֥וּם שִׁמְךָ֖ שָׁ֑ם לִשְׁמ֨וֹעַ֙ אֶל הַתְּפִלָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה

וְשָׁ֨מַעְתָּ֜ אֶל תַּחֲנוּנֵ֤י עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וּ אֶל הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְ֠אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַ֞ע מִמְּק֤וֹם שִׁבְתְּךָ֙ מִן הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ וְסָלָֽחְתָּ

וְ֠אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַ֨ע מִן הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם מְכ֤וֹן שִׁבְתֶּ֨ךָ֙ וְסָ֣לַחְתָּ֔ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה לָאִישׁ֙ כְּכָל דְּרָכָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּדַ֖ע אֶת לְבָב֑וֹ כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ לְבַדְּךָ֣ יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת לְבַ֖ב בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם

כָּל תְּפִלָּ֣ה כָל תְּחִנָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה֙ לְכָל הָ֣אָדָ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵדְע֗וּ אִ֤ישׁ נִגְעוֹ֙ וּמַכְאֹב֔וֹ וּפָרַ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה

leads.title: Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash ↔ Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Coronation in which the king receives the crown (nezer) and the 'testimony' (edut) (weight 7.7); King David's spears and shields kept in the temple are issued to the guards (weight 7.7); The temple of Baal is torn down and its priest slain before the altars (weight 7.7); A priest organizes the guards to overthrow a ruler and enthrone the hidden heir (weight 7.7); People acclaim 'Long live the king!' (weight 6.6). Pair score 37.6.

Only in Athaliah's usurpation and the hidden prince Joash: Deposed ruler tears her/his garments crying 'Conspiracy, conspiracy!' or 'Treason!'; A condemned person is taken out so as not to be killed inside the sanctuary; A covenant is made between God, the king and the people; The king stands by (or on) the pillar in the temple according to custom; A queen mother seizes power by killing all the royal offspring; Sole surviving royal infant is stolen away with his nurse and hidden in the temple for years; Men tear their garments in grief or dismay.

Only in Jehoiada's coup with the Levites; Joash crowned, Athaliah killed, Baal temple destroyed: After the usurper's execution the people rejoice and the city is quiet; A priestly coup is timed to the Sabbath change of temple guards, keeping both shifts; The newly crowned king stands by his pillar at the entrance; The usurper is led out so that she is not killed in the house of YHWH; The usurping queen tears her clothes and cries 'Treason, treason!'; Gatekeepers stationed so that no one unclean enters the temple; Those counted impure are kept out of the sanctuary [divergence between the texts]; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Invader promises deportees a land like their own, of grain, wine, oil and honey (weight 7.7); Officials ask the envoy to speak Aramaic, not Judean, so the people on the wall will not understand (weight 7.7); Invader claims the defenders' own god sent him to destroy the land (weight 7.7); Each man under his own vine and fig tree, drinking from his own cistern (weight 7.7); Enemy envoy addresses the besieged at the city wall to break their morale (weight 7.7); The people keep silent and do not answer the enemy at the king's command (weight 7.7); Threat that the besieged will eat their own dung and drink their urine (weight 7.3); Egypt likened to a broken reed staff that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it (weight 7.3); Taunt: Where are the gods of the conquered nations? Could they save their lands from my hand? (weight 6.8); An Assyrian king named in the narrative (Pul, Tiglath-pileser, Shalmaneser, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon) (weight 6.6); Command to smash altars, standing stones and Asherah poles and burn idols (weight 6.4); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 5.7). Pair score 86.7.

Only in Hezekiah's reform; Sennacherib's invasion and the Rabshakeh's speech: King smashes the bronze serpent made by Moses, called Nehushtan, because people burned incense to it; Image of a serpent on a pole heals those who look at it; A capital city is besieged for three years before it falls; King strips the temple and palace treasuries to buy off an invader; Conquered population deported to Assyria or another distant land; Formula: there was none like him among all the kings before or after.

Only in Sennacherib's invasion; the Rabshakeh's speech at the conduit: Prophet meets the king at the conduit of the upper pool on the highway of the Fuller's Field; Judah (or allies) put trust in Egypt and Cush for help against Assyria and are put to shame.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The king tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth and goes into the temple in crisis (weight 7.7); Proverb of crisis: children have come to the birth-stool and there is no strength to deliver (weight 7.7); Royal parricides flee to the land of Ararat (weight 7.7); God puts a spirit in the invader so that he hears a rumor and returns home (weight 7.7); The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses (weight 7.7); The arrogant king boasts of climbing the heights of Lebanon and cutting its cedars, drying up rivers with his feet (weight 7.7); The 'virgin daughter of Zion' laughs at and wags her head after the enemy (weight 7.7); Sign: this year eat aftergrowth, next year what springs of itself, the third year sow and reap (weight 7.7); God says the conqueror's victories were planned by him long ago; the conqueror is only his instrument (weight 7.7); The escaped remnant shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward; a remnant goes out from Zion (weight 7.7); King spreads the enemy's threatening letter before God in the temple (weight 7.7); God's angels strike the enemy army [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); The enemy is said to reproach (harref) 'the living God' (weight 7.3); Enemy king is murdered by his own sons while worshipping in his god's temple (weight 7.1); God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant (weight 7.1); God will put his hook in the enemy king's nose and his bit in his lips and lead him back (weight 6.8); Conquered nations' gods were burned because they were no gods, only wood and stone made by hands (weight 6.8); Taunt: Where are the gods of the conquered nations? Could they save their lands from my hand? (weight 6.8); God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim (weight 6.5). Pair score 141.0.

Only in Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter: God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant [divergence between the texts]; When the punishment descends in their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned; Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings.

Only in Hezekiah's prayer, Isaiah's oracle against Sennacherib and the angel's slaughter: The angel of YHWH strikes 185,000 in the enemy camp in one night; at dawn all are corpses [divergence between the texts]; 'The zeal of YHWH of hosts will accomplish this'; A remnant that survives judgment will be called holy and restored.

leads.title: Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys ↔ Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm
leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Given a choice of signs, the king picks the harder (shadow going backward) (weight 7.7); Prophet tells the sick king 'Set your house in order, for you shall die' (weight 7.7); A cake of figs laid on a boil heals the king (weight 7.7); Dying man turns his face to the wall and prays, weeping (weight 7.7); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.3); In answer to prayer God adds fifteen years to the king's life (weight 7.3); As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz (weight 7.3); At a leader's command the sun and moon stand still until the battle is won (weight 7.1). Pair score 60.1.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps and the Babylonian envoys: The king proudly shows foreign envoys all his treasures, prompting a prophecy of their loss; A king receives a foreign ruler's envoys and gift [contrast between the texts]; King accepts doom for his descendants, glad there will be peace and truth in his own days; Prophecy that the king's descendants will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon; King makes a pool and conduit to bring water into the city; God defends the city for his own sake and for the sake of David his servant.

Only in Hezekiah's illness, the shadow on the steps of Ahaz, and Hezekiah's psalm: Speaker laments that in the noon of his days he must go to the gates of Sheol, deprived of the rest of his years; A psalm-like 'writing' (mikhtav) of the king composed when he was sick and recovered; My dwelling is pulled up like a shepherd's tent; I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off from the loom; God has cast all the speaker's sins behind his back and held back his soul from the pit of destruction; The dead cannot praise God: no wonders for the dead, no hesed in the grave, no faithfulness in Abaddon; A dying person's plea to God for more life, and God's answer [contrast between the texts]; On that day neither wealth nor sons avail, only one who comes to God with a sound heart; Bequest (wasiyya) to parents and kin prescribed for one who leaves wealth; altering it is a sin; In distress the sufferer chirps like a swift or crane and moans like a dove; Death or Sheol has gates (sha'arei mavet).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Royal officials consult a woman prophet on behalf of the king (weight 6.7); A lost book of the law is found in the temple during repairs (weight 6.7); Because the king humbled himself, he will die in peace and not see the coming disaster (weight 6.7); Workmen handling sacred funds are not audited because they deal faithfully (weight 6.3); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 4.9). Pair score 31.3.

Only in Josiah's temple repair, the finding of the book and Huldah's oracle: A newly found sacred book is read aloud before the king, who tears his clothes; The king organizes the collection of silver for repairing the temple; A child of eight to twelve years becomes king.

Only in Temple repair, finding of the book of the Torah, Huldah's oracle and covenant: Prophet announces that the curses written in the found book will come upon the land; King stands at his place and makes the covenant before God; Levites skilled in music oversee the burden-bearers and workmen; The scribe reads the found book aloud before the king; Money collected by the Levites is given to the workmen to repair the temple; The book of the covenant is read aloud to the people; King and people enter a covenant to seek or serve YHWH in a public ceremony.

Only in The siege and destruction of Jerusalem; Gedaliah; Jehoiachin released: Exiled king's head is 'lifted up' from prison; he changes his prison garments and eats at the conqueror's table; Temple pillars eighteen cubits high with bronze capitals, network and pomegranates; Only the poorest of the land are left behind as vinedressers and farmers; The temple, palace and great houses are burned by the conqueror's chief of guards (rav tabbahim); The bronze pillars, stands and sea are broken up and their bronze carried away; A governor appointed by the conqueror is assassinated by a member of the royal seed; The remnant flees to Egypt for fear of the conquerors (reverse exodus); Siege of Jerusalem begun on the tenth day of the tenth month (later a fast day); Captive's eyes are gouged out by his captors.

Only in David's song of deliverance (= Psalm 18): Theophany with thunder, lightning, thick cloud and a loud trumpet; Leader and people sing a victory song after the enemy's destruction; God called the Rock (tsur).

Only in Psalm 18 - David's song of deliverance and the storm theophany: God makes darkness his hiding place and dark waters and clouds his canopy; The king gives thanks for God's deliverance from all his enemies (song also in 2 Sam 22); At God's rebuke the channels of the sea are seen and the foundations of the world laid bare; 'Who is God except YHWH, and who is a rock besides our God?'; God answers the distressed when he calls and removes the evil; God's words are pure, silver refined in a furnace, purified seven times; God addressed with a string of protective epithets: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn of salvation, stronghold; Thunder is the roaring voice of God; On that day a great earthquake shakes the land; fish, birds, beasts, creeping things and all humans quake before God, mountains are thrown down and every wall falls; God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven; Superscription sets the psalm in a specific episode of David's life.

leads.title: David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor ↔ Satan incites the census; plague, the angel over Jerusalem and Ornan's threshing floor
leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A prophet offers the king a choice among three punishments (weight 7.7); The king refuses a free gift of land for an altar and pays its price (weight 7.7); King asks that punishment fall on him and his house rather than on the innocent 'sheep' (weight 7.7); A threshing floor where the plague was stopped becomes the site of the altar and temple (weight 7.1); Exact number of dead in a divine plague is given (weight 7.1); Hero's prayer or act halts a divine punishment (weight 6.2). Pair score 43.6.

Only in David's census, the plague, and Araunah's threshing floor: Itinerary of census-takers around the land's borders; The king's heart strikes him after a sin; The commander objects to the king's census; Counting the people requires a ransom for each life to avert plague; God halts the destroying angel at a specific spot: 'Enough, stay your hand'; God himself incites a person to an evil act; The believers' pride in their great numbers avails nothing and the earth grows narrow for them (Hunayn); Census totals given tribe by tribe.

Only in Satan incites the census; plague, the angel over Jerusalem and Ornan's threshing floor: The angel of YHWH is seen standing between earth and heaven; At God's command the destroying angel returns his sword to its sheath; A destroying angel (mal'akh mashhit) is sent against the land or city; King and elders clothed in sackcloth fall on their faces before the angel; Let me fall into the hand of God, whose mercies are great, and not into the hand of man; The whole land 'from Beersheba to Dan'; The commander protests the king's order but is overruled; The landowner sees the angel while threshing and his sons hide; Satan (or an adversary) stands up against Israel and incites the king to sin; A king's census of the people is a sin that brings punishment; You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love; Angel of YHWH stands in the way with a drawn sword; and 5 more.

passages.text: הָל֞וֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֶל דָּוִ֗ד כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁלֹ֕שׁ אָנֹכִ֖י נוֹטֵ֣ל עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר לְךָ֥ אַֽחַת מֵהֶ֖ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּֽךְ

וַיָּבֹא גָ֥ד אֶל דָּוִ֖ד וַיַּגֶּד ל֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֡וֹ הֲתָב֣וֹא לְךָ֣ שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֣ים רָעָ֣ב בְּאַרְצֶ֡ךָ אִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳ֠דָשִׁים נֻסְךָ֨ לִפְנֵֽי צָרֶ֜יךָ וְה֣וּא רֹדְפֶ֗ךָ וְאִם הֱ֠יוֹת שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת יָמִ֥ים דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּאַרְצֶ֔ךָ עַתָּה֙ דַּ֣ע וּרְאֵ֔ה מָה אָשִׁ֥יב שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר
וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל גָּ֖ד צַר לִ֣י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְּלָה נָּ֤א בְיַד יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי רַבִּ֣ים רחמו רַֽחֲמָ֔יו וּבְיַד אָדָ֖ם אַל אֶפֹּֽלָה

sides.note: Seven years famine, three months flight, three days pestilence; 'let me fall into the hand of YHWH, for his mercies are great'

passages.text: לֵךְ֩ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֶל דָּוִ֜יד לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁל֕וֹשׁ אֲנִ֖י נֹטֶ֣ה עָלֶ֑יךָ בְּחַר לְךָ֛ אַחַ֥ת מֵהֵ֖נָּה וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּֽךְ
וַיָּ֥בֹא גָ֖ד אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה קַבֶּל לָֽךְ

אִם שָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים רָעָ֗ב וְאִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה חֳדָשִׁ֜ים נִסְפֶּ֥ה מִפְּנֵי צָרֶיךָ֮ וְחֶ֣רֶב אוֹיְבֶ֣ךָ לְמַשֶּׂגֶת֒ וְאִם שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָ֠מִים חֶ֣רֶב יְהוָ֤ה וְדֶ֨בֶר֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה מַשְׁחִ֖ית בְּכָל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֣ה רְאֵ֔ה מָֽה אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שֹׁלְחִ֖י דָּבָֽר

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֨וְנָה֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד יִקַּ֥ח וְיַ֛עַל אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב בעינו בְּעֵינָ֑יו רְאֵה֙ הַבָּקָ֣ר לָעֹלָ֔ה וְהַמֹּרִגִּ֛ים וּכְלֵ֥י הַבָּקָ֖ר לָעֵצִֽים
הַכֹּ֗ל נָתַ֛ן אֲרַ֥וְנָה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲרַ֨וְנָה֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִרְצֶֽךָ

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל אֲרַ֗וְנָה לֹ֚א כִּֽי קָנ֨וֹ אֶקְנֶ֤ה מֵאֽוֹתְךָ֙ בִּמְחִ֔יר וְלֹ֧א אַעֲלֶ֛ה לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖י עֹל֣וֹת חִנָּ֑ם וַיִּ֨קֶן דָּוִ֤ד אֶת הַגֹּ֨רֶן֙ וְאֶת הַבָּקָ֔ר בְּכֶ֖סֶף שְׁקָלִ֥ים חֲמִשִּֽׁים

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜יד אֶל אָרְנָ֗ן תְּנָה לִּי֙ מְק֣וֹם הַגֹּ֔רֶן וְאֶבְנֶה בּ֥וֹ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה בְּכֶ֤סֶף מָלֵא֙ תְּנֵ֣הוּ לִ֔י וְתֵעָצַ֥ר הַמַּגֵּפָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל הָעָֽם

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אָרְנָ֤ן אֶל דָּוִיד֙ קַֽח לָ֔ךְ וְיַ֛עַשׂ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינָ֑יו רְאֵה֩ נָתַ֨תִּי הַבָּקָ֜ר לָֽעֹל֗וֹת וְהַמּוֹרִגִּ֧ים לָעֵצִ֛ים וְהַחִטִּ֥ים לַמִּנְחָ֖ה הַכֹּ֥ל נָתָֽתִּי
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ לְאָרְנָ֔ן לֹ֕א כִּֽי קָנֹ֥ה אֶקְנֶ֖ה בְּכֶ֣סֶף מָלֵ֑א כִּ֠י לֹא אֶשָּׂ֤א אֲשֶׁר לְךָ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וְהַעֲל֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ה חִנָּֽם
