evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The ark is carried on a new cart drawn by oxen (weight 7.7); The ark stays three months in a foreigner's house and God blesses his household (weight 7.7); A man who reaches out to steady the ark when the oxen stumble is struck dead (weight 7.7); The ark is brought up in procession with singing, lyres, harps, drums, cymbals and trumpets (weight 7.3); Kiriath-jearim also called Baalah or Kiriath-baal (weight 7.1); God addressed as enthroned (yoshev) on the cherubim (weight 6.5). Pair score 44.1.

Only in The ark brought to Jerusalem; Uzzah struck; David dances; Michal despises him: The ark is set in a tent the king pitched for it; The king blesses the people and gives each person bread and cakes; The king dances with all his might, girded in a linen ephod; A sacrifice offered after the first six steps of the bearers; A wife mocks her husband for exposing himself while dancing; Offenders punished by dying childless; A woman looks out through the window lattice; A place is named after an event that happened there, 'to this day'.

Only in The first attempt to bring up the ark; Uzza struck down: A place is named for God's 'breaking out' (perets) against someone (Perez-uzza, Baal-perazim); Witness fears he will die because he has seen God or an angel.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A prophet approves a plan, then is corrected by a revelation that night (weight 7.7); Israel is the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem for himself (weight 7.7); God promises to make the chosen one's name great (weight 7.7); God has never dwelt in a house but moved from tent to tent (weight 7.7); God took the ruler from following the sheep (weight 7.7); Prayer of humility: 'Who am I and what is my house?' (weight 7.7); The king's son, not the king, will build the house for God's name (weight 7.3); God declares the king his son: 'I will be his father and he my son' (weight 7.1); God promises David's house and throne will endure forever (weight 6.6). Pair score 67.5.

Only in Nathan's oracle of the eternal house of David and David's prayer: God's steadfast love will not be withdrawn from the heir as it was from the previous king; Obscure phrase 'this is the torah of man (adam)'; Wordplay on 'house' as temple and as dynasty; Whether God has, begets or takes sons or other offspring [contrast between the texts]; God disciplines Israel as a man disciplines his son; Whether God has a son, or calls his anointed king his begotten son [contrast between the texts]; The king, living in a cedar palace, proposes to build a house for God; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in Nathan's oracle of an eternal house and David's prayer: Pun on 'house': the king would build God a house; God will build the king a house (dynasty); Revelation described as God 'uncovering the ear' of his servant; The king lives in a cedar house while the ark of God remains under curtains; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A neighboring king sends his son with precious vessels to congratulate the victor (weight 7.7); A battle in the Valley of Salt (weight 7.7); List of the king's chief officials: commander, recorder, priests, scribe, guard (weight 7.3); Shields of beaten gold made or captured and displayed (weight 7.3); The enemy's horses are hamstrung and their chariots burned by divine command (weight 7.1); The king dedicates silver and gold from conquered nations to God (weight 6.5); Subject peoples bring tribute (minhah) to the king (weight 6.5); The king does justice and righteousness for all his people (weight 5.4). Pair score 55.7.

Only in David's conquests and list of officials: Captives laid on the ground and measured with a cord to decide who is killed; The Euphrates as the limit of the king's dominion; Obscure term 'Metheg-ammah' for what David took from the Philistines; The king's sons serve as priests.

Only in David's conquests and his officials: The Cherethite and Pelethite royal guard; A king goes to 'set up his hand' (monument) at the Euphrates; Bronze captured in war used for the temple's sea, pillars and vessels; Chronicles differs in a specific detail from its parallel in Samuel–Kings.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: People fear to hear God directly and ask the prophet to mediate (weight 7.3); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); No other gods before YHWH (weight 6.8); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.8); Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers (weight 6.6); Prohibition of carved images or likenesses of anything for worship (weight 6.6); God visits the fathers' sin on the third and fourth generation, but keeps steadfast love for thousands (weight 6.5); The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) (weight 6.5); Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property (weight 6.2); Honor father and mother, with the promise of long life (weight 5.9); Prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft and false witness (weight 5.7). Pair score 72.1.

Only in The Ten Words and the people's fear: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the house of slaves; The people 'see' the voices or thunder at the revelation; The prophet approaches the thick darkness where God is; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden [divergence between the texts]; Prohibition of coveting the neighbor's wife and property [divergence between the texts]; Do not kill the soul God has made sacred except by right [divergence between the texts]; No other gods before YHWH [divergence between the texts]; The ground and the reward of the duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; The Sabbath is justified by God's resting on the seventh day of creation; The Sabbath was imposed only on those who differed about it [response between the texts]; The Ten Commandments (Decalogue) [divergence between the texts]; Do not stretch your eyes toward the worldly splendor given to others to test them; and 3 more.

Only in The Decalogue restated and the people's fear at Horeb: The covenant is made with those alive today, not only with the fathers; Worship of God alone joined to duty to parents [divergence between the texts]; Whether God should speak to the people directly [contrast between the texts]; Mountain burns with fire to the heart of heaven amid darkness and cloud; The people answer as one: all that YHWH has spoken we will do [response between the texts]; Who was present at the revelation on the mountain, and who knows it only by report [contrast between the texts]; God heard as a voice out of fire with no visible form; The people's answer to the covenant ('we hear ...') [response between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; Believers' confession 'we hear and we obey' (sami'na wa-ata'na); Keep the law, turning neither to the right nor to the left; God gives stone tablets he himself has written.

וְעַתָּה֙ לָ֣מָּה נָמ֔וּת כִּ֣י תֹֽאכְלֵ֔נוּ הָאֵ֥שׁ הַגְּדֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את אִם יֹסְפִ֣ים אֲנַ֗חְנוּ לִ֠שְׁמֹעַ אֶת ק֨וֹל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ ע֖וֹד וָמָֽתְנוּ

sides.note: who of all flesh has heard the voice of the living God and lived

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֥ד אֶת אָבִ֖יךָ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יַאֲרִכ֣וּן יָמֶ֔יךָ עַ֚ל הָאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

sides.note: kabbēd ʾet-ʾābîkā wəʾet-ʾimmekā ləmaʿan yaʾărikûn yāmêkā; wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan immā yablughanna ʿindaka l-kibara ... fa-lā taqul lahumā uffin ... wa-qul rabbi rḥamhumā ka-mā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. Q drops the promise of long life and puts in its place care for parents in old age and a prayer for them. Duty to parents comes second, right after God, in both.

passages.text: כַּבֵּ֤ד אֶת אָבִ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת אִמֶּ֔ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לְמַ֣עַן יַאֲרִיכֻ֣ן יָמֶ֗יךָ וּלְמַ֨עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ

sides.note: Deut: kabbēd ʾet-ʾāvîkhā wə-ʾet-ʾimmekhā ... ləmaʿan yaʾărîkhūn yāmêkhā û-ləmaʿan yîṭav lākh ʿal-hā-ʾădāmāh. Q: wa-bi-l-wālidayni iḥsānan. 'Honour' becomes 'kindness', and the promise of long life in the land is dropped.

matches.label: No other gods before YHWH

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
לֹא יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ

sides.note: Q: wa-mā min ilāhin illā ilāhun wāḥidun; man yushrik bi-llāhi fa-qad ḥarrama llāhu ʿalayhi l-janna. Deut: lōʾ yihyeh-ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ʿal-pānāy. Q has Jesus himself proclaim it (uʿbudū llāha rabbī wa-rabbakum).

passages.text: לֹֽ֣א יִהְיֶֽה לְךָ֛ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים עַל פָּנָֽיַ
לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
לֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף

sides.note: The same sequence: no other god, no killing, no adultery, no false witness: lā yadʿūna maʿa llāhi ilāhan ākhara wa-lā yaqtulūna n-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi wa-lā yaznūna ... lā yashhadūna z-zūra ~ lōʾ yihyeh ləkhā ʾĕlōhîm ʾăḥērîm ... lōʾ tirṣāḥ lōʾ tinʾāf ... lōʾ taʿăneh və-rēʿăkā ʿēd šāqer. Changes: the absolute lōʾ tirṣāḥ gets an exception ('except by right', illā bi-l-ḥaqq); theft is left out; the commands become a description of the righteous (alladhīna lā ...), followed by doubled punishment and an exception for those who repent (25:69-70).

passages.text: לֹ֖א תִּרְצָֽח
וְלֹ֖א תִּנְאָֽף
וְלֹֽא תַעֲנֶ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָ֖ עֵ֥ד שָֽׁוְא

sides.note: Deut: lōʾ tirṣāḥ; wə-lōʾ tinʾāf; wə-lōʾ-taʿăneh və-rēʿăkhā ʿēd šāwʾ, absolute. Q qualifies and widens: wa-lā taqtulū l-nafsa llatī ḥarrama llāhu illā bi-l-ḥaqqi (with an exception); wa-lā taqrabū l-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa-mā baṭana (all indecency, not only adultery); wa-idhā qultum fa-ʿdilū wa-law kāna dhā qurbā (just speech even against kin). Theft is absent.

זָכ֛וֹר אֶת י֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֖ת לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ
וְי֨וֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽ֣א תַעֲשֶׂ֨ה כָל מְלָאכָ֜ה אַתָּ֣ה וּבִנְךָֽ֣ וּבִתֶּ֗ךָ עַבְדְּךָ֤ וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ וּבְהֶמְתֶּ֔ךָ וְגֵרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ

leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning (weight 7.7); No one shall appear before God empty-handed (weight 7.7); How often and when pilgrimage is made [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk (weight 7.1); Three annual pilgrimage festivals when every male appears before God (weight 6.4); Bring the first fruits of the land to the house of God (weight 5.8). Pair score 42.0.

Only in Covenant Code - justice, enemy's animal, sabbatical year, festivals: Return your enemy's stray animal and help his overloaded donkey; Neither favor nor pervert justice for the poor in his lawsuit; Whoever commits a sin and casts it on an innocent bears slander and manifest sin; God does not forbid kindness and justice toward those who did not fight you over religion or expel you; The land lies fallow in the seventh year for the poor and wild animals; Do not invoke the names of other gods; Let not hatred of a people move you to injustice; be just; Do not spread false reports or follow the majority to do wrong in court; Who must make pilgrimage to the sanctuary, and how often [divergence between the texts]; Do not oppress the stranger, for you were strangers in Egypt; Sabbath rest on the seventh day for all, including servants, animals and strangers; Judge fairly, favoring neither the poor nor the great; and 1 more.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; How far God's mercy and his punishment extend [divergence between the texts]; Moses hews a second pair of tablets to replace the broken ones; Treaties with idolatrous peoples [contrast between the texts]; and 16 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A cult object is hammered from a single piece of gold (weight 7.7); A golden cover (kapporet, mercy seat) on top of the ark (weight 7.7); A golden seven-lamp lampstand with almond-blossom cups (weight 7.1); A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God (weight 6.8); The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles (weight 6.6); Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark (weight 6.5). Pair score 42.5.

Only in Contribution for the sanctuary; ark, cover, table and lampstand: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles [divergence between the texts]; List of precious materials for the sanctuary: metals, dyed yarns, linen, skins, wood, oil, spices, gems; God's voice speaks to Moses from above the ark cover between the two cherubim; The ark's carrying poles must never be removed; God will dwell in the midst of the people in a sanctuary; Exact dimensions in cubits are given for a sacred object of the sanctuary; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); Materials for the sanctuary come from the free-will gifts of all whose heart moves them; The tablets of the testimony are placed inside the ark; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

passages.text: (25:31) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מְנֹרַ֖ת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה תֵּעָשֶׂ֤ה הַמְּנוֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יִהְיֽוּ (25:32) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (25:33) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בַּקָּנֶ֥ה הָאֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:34) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (25:35) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (25:36) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:37) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ (25:38) וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (25:39) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

passages.text: (37:17) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַמְּנֹרָ֖ה זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר מִקְשָׁ֞ה עָשָׂ֤ה אֶת הַמְּנֹרָה֙ יְרֵכָ֣הּ וְקָנָ֔הּ גְּבִיעֶ֛יהָ כַּפְתֹּרֶ֥יהָ וּפְרָחֶ֖יהָ מִמֶּ֥נָּה הָיֽוּ (37:18) וְשִׁשָּׁ֣ה קָנִ֔ים יֹצְאִ֖ים מִצִּדֶּ֑יהָ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֗ה מִצִּדָּהּ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ קְנֵ֣י מְנֹרָ֔ה מִצִּדָּ֖הּ הַשֵּׁנִֽי (37:19) שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְ֠בִעִים מְֽשֻׁקָּדִ֞ים בַּקָּנֶ֣ה הָאֶחָד֮ כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפֶרַח֒ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה גְבִעִ֗ים מְשֻׁקָּדִ֛ים בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד כַּפְתֹּ֣ר וָפָ֑רַח כֵּ֚ן לְשֵׁ֣שֶׁת הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִן הַמְּנֹרָֽה (37:20) וּבַמְּנֹרָ֖ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה גְבִעִ֑ים מְשֻׁ֨קָּדִ֔ים כַּפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ וּפְרָחֶֽיהָ (37:21) וְכַפְתֹּ֡ר תַּחַת֩ שְׁנֵ֨י הַקָּנִ֜ים מִמֶּ֗נָּה וְכַפְתֹּר֙ תַּ֣חַת שְׁנֵ֤י הַקָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְכַפְתֹּ֕ר תַּֽחַת שְׁנֵ֥י הַקָּנִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑נָּה לְשֵׁ֨שֶׁת֙ הַקָּנִ֔ים הַיֹּצְאִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנָּה (37:22) כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה הָי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:23) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר (37:24) כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר עָשָׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ וְאֵ֖ת כָּל כֵּלֶֽיהָ

matches.label: A gold table with the bread of the presence always before God

passages.text: (25:23) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:24) וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ לּ֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:25) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ לּ֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (25:26) וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (25:27) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת לְבָתִּ֣ים לְבַדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:28) וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְנִשָּׂא בָ֖ם אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (25:29) וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ קְּעָרֹתָ֜יו וְכַפֹּתָ֗יו וּקְשׂוֹתָיו֙ וּמְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם (25:30) וְנָתַתָּ֧ עַֽל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן לֶ֥חֶם פָּנִ֖ים לְפָנַ֥י תָּמִֽיד

sides.note: lehem panim 'bread of the face' always before me

passages.text: (37:10) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּוֹ֙ וְאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:11) וַיְצַ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:12) וַיַּ֨עַשׂ ל֥וֹ מִסְגֶּ֛רֶת טֹ֖פַח סָבִ֑יב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ זֵר זָהָ֛ב לְמִסְגַּרְתּ֖וֹ סָבִֽיב (37:13) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֔וֹ אַרְבַּ֖ע טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֑ב וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע הַפֵּאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְאַרְבַּ֥ע רַגְלָֽיו (37:14) לְעֻמַּת֙ הַמִּסְגֶּ֔רֶת הָי֖וּ הַטַּבָּעֹ֑ת בָּתִּים֙ לַבַּדִּ֔ים לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:15) וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָ֑ב לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הַשֻּׁלְחָֽן (37:16) וַיַּ֜עַשׂ אֶֽת הַכֵּלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֶת קְעָרֹתָ֤יו וְאֶת כַּפֹּתָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ מְנַקִּיֹּתָ֔יו וְאֶת הַקְּשָׂוֺ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻסַּ֖ךְ בָּהֵ֑ן זָהָ֖ב טָהֽוֹר

matches.label: The ark of the covenant: a gold-plated acacia chest with rings and poles

passages.text: (25:10) וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (25:11) וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתוֹ֙ זָהָ֣ב טָה֔וֹר מִבַּ֥יִת וּמִח֖וּץ תְּצַפֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָשִׂ֧יתָ עָלָ֛יו זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (25:12) וְיָצַ֣קְתָּ לּ֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב וְנָ֣תַתָּ֔ה עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּעֹ֔ת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (25:13) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בַדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (25:14) וְהֵֽבֵאתָ֤ אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֥את אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן בָּהֶֽם (25:15) בְּטַבְּעֹת֙ הָאָרֹ֔ן יִהְי֖וּ הַבַּדִּ֑ים לֹ֥א יָסֻ֖רוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ (25:16) וְנָתַתָּ֖ אֶל הָאָרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָעֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶתֵּ֖ן אֵלֶֽיךָ

(37:1) וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ (37:2) וַיְצַפֵּ֛הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר מִבַּ֣יִת וּמִח֑וּץ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ זֵ֥ר זָהָ֖ב סָבִֽיב (37:3) וַיִּצֹ֣ק ל֗וֹ אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פַּעֲמֹתָ֑יו וּשְׁתֵּ֣י טַבָּעֹ֗ת עַל צַלְעוֹ֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּי֙ טַבָּע֔וֹת עַל צַלְע֖וֹ הַשֵּׁנִֽית (37:4) וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וַיְצַ֥ף אֹתָ֖ם זָהָֽב (37:5) וַיָּבֵ֤א אֶת הַבַּדִּים֙ בַּטַּבָּעֹ֔ת עַ֖ל צַלְעֹ֣ת הָאָרֹ֑ן לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת הָאָרֹֽן
וַיַּ֧עַשׂ בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל אֶת הָאָרֹ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָחֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְאַמָּ֤ה וָחֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמָּ֥ה וָחֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽוֹ

matches.label: Two golden cherubim face each other with wings spread over the ark

passages.text: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ שְׁנַ֥יִם כְּרֻבִ֖ים זָהָ֑ב מִקְשָׁה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֔ם מִשְּׁנֵ֖י קְצ֥וֹת הַכַּפֹּֽרֶת
וַ֠עֲשֵׂה כְּר֨וּב אֶחָ֤ד מִקָּצָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וּכְרוּב אֶחָ֥ד מִקָּצָ֖ה מִזֶּ֑ה מִן הַכַּפֹּ֛רֶת תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֶת הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עַל שְׁנֵ֥י קְצוֹתָֽיו
וְהָי֣וּ הַכְּרֻבִים֩ פֹּרְשֵׂ֨י כְנָפַ֜יִם לְמַ֗עְלָה סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל אָחִ֑יו אֶל הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת יִהְי֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A middle bar runs through the frames from end to end (weight 7.7); An embroidered screen at the entrance of the tent or court (weight 7.7); Tabernacle walls of acacia frames set in silver sockets (weight 7.7); Eleven goat-hair curtains form the tent over the tabernacle (weight 7.7); Outer coverings of red-dyed ram skins and tahash skins (weight 7.7); Curtains joined by fifty loops and fifty clasps (weight 7.7); A veil (parokhet) divides the holy place from the holy of holies (weight 7.3); Tabernacle curtains or veil woven with cherubim (weight 7.3). Pair score 61.2.

Only in Tabernacle curtains, frames and veil: The lampstand stands on the south side and the table on the north; Covering of tahash skins (an unidentified animal); The innermost room, the holy of holies, holds the ark; The sanctuary is built after a pattern shown by God on the mountain.

Only in Bezalel appointed; too many gifts; making of the curtains and frames: God gives the master craftsmen the ability to teach others; The people bring more than enough and must be told to stop giving; God calls a master craftsman by name for the sacred work; A second craftsman from the tribe of Dan assists the master craftsman; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לַמָּסָ֗ךְ חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתָם֙ זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְיָצַקְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אַדְנֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת

passages.text: (26:15) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים (26:16) עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:17) שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן (26:18) וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (26:19) וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו (26:20) וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ (26:21) וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד (26:22) וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים (26:23) וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם (26:24) וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ (26:25) וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד

leads.summary: 8 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The priest carries Israel's names before God as a memorial (weight 7.7); The robe's neck opening is bound so it will not tear (weight 7.7); The priest's robe has gold bells and pomegranates on its hem so he does not die (weight 7.7); The names of the twelve tribes are engraved like seals on gemstones (weight 7.7); Priests wear linen breeches to cover their nakedness, on pain of death (weight 7.3); The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces (weight 7.3); The breastpiece of judgment set with twelve gems in four rows (weight 7.3); A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead (weight 7.1). Pair score 60.1.

Only in The high priest's vestments: Aaron and his sons are designated as priests; Priestly garments are made for glory and beauty; Priests are installed by anointing and 'filling the hand'; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; God fills craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom for sacred work.

Only in The vestments made; the work completed and blessed: Gold is beaten into sheets and cut into threads for weaving; The leader sees the finished work and blesses the workers; Completion of the sanctuary is narrated in the language of the completion of creation; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Ordination of priests lasts seven days (weight 7.7); Blood and anointing oil are sprinkled on the priests and their garments (weight 7.7); Priests are washed with water at the entrance before ordination (weight 7.3); Anointing oil is poured on the head of the priest (weight 7.3); Blood is daubed on the right earlobe, thumb and big toe (weight 7.3); Sacred meat left over until morning is burned (weight 7.3); Portions are waved before God as a wave offering (weight 7.3); The offerer lays his hand on the head of the animal (weight 6.8); The flesh, skin and dung of the sin offering are burned outside the camp (weight 6.8); Blood is put on the horns of the altar with the finger and poured at its base (weight 6.8). Pair score 72.7.

Only in Ordination of the priests: A basket of unleavened bread, oiled cakes and wafers is offered; An outsider may not eat holy food; The high priest's vestments pass to his successor, who wears them seven days; The breast and the right thigh are the priests' portion; Whatever touches the most holy altar or holy things becomes holy; Sacrificial animals must be without blemish; The fat, the two kidneys and the lobe of the liver are burned on the altar; The fat tail of the sheep is offered; An offering by fire is a pleasing odor to God.

Only in Moses ordains Aaron and his sons: Moses himself performs the priestly rites at the ordination; The whole congregation is assembled at the tent entrance to witness a rite; Anointing makes the tent and its furnishings holy; The refrain 'as YHWH commanded Moses' recurs in a sevenfold pattern; The ephod, a woven priestly garment with shoulder pieces; Urim and Thummim placed in the breastpiece for divine decision; Execution of a divine command is narrated by repeating the command almost verbatim; A gold plate engraved 'Holy to YHWH' on the priest's forehead; A ritual action is performed seven times.

leads.title: Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey ↔ Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house
leads.summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A spirit enters the prophet and sets him on his feet (weight 7.7); Israel called 'a rebellious house' (beit meri) (weight 7.7); The prophet sees 'the likeness of the glory of YHWH' as radiant fire enthroned (weight 7.3); The prophet must speak 'whether they hear or refuse' (weight 7.3); 'The hand of YHWH was upon' the prophet, bringing a vision or transport (weight 7.3). Pair score 37.5.

Only in Ezekiel's commission as 'son of man' to the rebellious house; he eats the scroll sweet as honey: Heavenly voice cries 'Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place'; God makes the prophet's forehead as hard as diamond against a hard-faced people; Foreign peoples of strange speech would heed the prophet, but Israel will not; A hand is stretched out to the prophet holding a scroll; The prophet is made to eat a heavenly scroll; God addresses the prophet as 'son of man' (ben adam); The prophet lives among briers, thorns and scorpions, yet must not fear; The spirit lifts and carries the prophet away; After his vision the prophet sits stunned among the people for seven days; A great rushing sound of the creatures' wings and the wheels behind the prophet; The eaten scroll tastes sweet as honey in the prophet's mouth; A scroll written on front and back with laments, mourning and woe; and 5 more.

Only in Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house: The glory seen by the river appears again to the prophet in a valley/plain; The prophet is told to shut himself in his house; If the watchman fails to warn the wicked, God requires their blood from him; Muteness imposed as a sign [divergence between the texts]; A righteous man who turns to iniquity dies and his former righteousness is not remembered; God appoints the prophet as a watchman (tsofeh) for the house of Israel; God makes the prophet's tongue cleave to his palate so he is mute except when God speaks; The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory; Each person dies for his own sin.

Only in Generations of Esau, Horite chiefs, kings of Edom: Amalek's ancestor is born to a concubine in Esau's line; Brothers separate because the land cannot support both their herds; While herding his father's asses, a man discovers 'the yemim' in the wilderness (hot springs or mules).

Only in Sons of Ishmael, Keturah and Esau; the Seirite chiefs and kings of Edom: Abraham's sons by the concubine Keturah (Midian, Sheba, Dedan...); Ishmael promised to father twelve princes and a great nation; Ishmael's twelve sons as Arabian tribes (Nebaioth, Kedar, Dumah, Tema...); A lone daughter is named in a male genealogy (Dinah, Serah).

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The conqueror leaves the poorest people in the land as vinedressers and farmers (weight 7.7); Jerusalem is breached, captured and burned by the Babylonians (weight 7.7); The fleeing king is overtaken in the plains of Jericho (weight 7.7); The captive king's sons are slaughtered before his eyes, then his eyes are put out (weight 7.3); Besieged king flees by night through a gate between the walls and is overtaken (weight 7.3). Pair score 37.9.

Only in Fall of Jerusalem; Zedekiah blinded at Riblah; Jeremiah freed; Ebed-melech promised safety: The conquering Babylonian officers, named with their titles (Rab-saris, Rab-mag), sit in the city's Middle Gate; The foreign conqueror orders his officers to look after the prophet and do him no harm; A foreigner who helped the prophet is promised his life will be spared because he trusted God; Whoever surrenders to the enemy will live; his life shall be his booty; Captive king taken with hooks and bound in bronze fetters to Babylon.

Only in Historical appendix: siege, burning of the temple, bronze spoils, deportation numbers, Jehoiachin's release: A captive king is released after decades, changes his prison clothes and eats at the foreign king's table; A king 'lifts the head' of a prisoner, releasing and honoring him; The besiegers build a siege wall (dayeq) around the city; The chief priest, second priest and officials are executed by the conqueror at Riblah; The king's mother is named in his regnal formula; The released captive king is given a throne above the other kings in Babylon; The temple of Jerusalem is burned and the city walls broken down; Precise numbers of deportees for each year of exile; Seven princes or counselors who 'see the king's face' advise the king; Two named bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, before the temple; The temple treasures and gold vessels of Solomon are carried off to Babylon; A great cast-bronze 'sea' basin rests on twelve bronze oxen facing the four directions in threes; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A conquered nation's god goes into exile with his priests and princes (weight 7.7); The enemy swoops like an eagle and spreads its wings over a land (weight 7.7); God will restore the fortunes of a foreign nation in the latter days (weight 7.7); The heart of warriors on that day is like the heart of a woman in labor (weight 7.7); Brief oracles against neighboring nations (Amalek, Kenite, Asshur, Kittim) (weight 5.7). Only in Oracle against Moab: wine settled on its lees, Chemosh into exile: Lament: how the mighty staff, the glorious rod, is broken; The nation is broken like a vessel no one wants; Long list of Moabite towns under judgment (Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, Bozrah...); Cursed is he who does YHWH's work slackly and keeps his sword from blood; Refugees told to dwell in the rocks like a dove nesting in the sides of a gorge; 'Give wings to Moab', for she must flee away; The joyful 'hedad' shout of grape-treaders falls silent; Fugitives become like a juniper (or wild ass) in the desert; A nation made drunk wallows in its vomit and becomes a laughing-stock; The great pride, arrogance and haughtiness of Moab; The vine of Sibmah whose tendrils crossed the sea, now despoiled; A nation at ease like wine settled on its lees, never poured from vessel to vessel; and 6 more.

Only in Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, and Elam: Desert peoples described as those with the corners of their hair clipped; A people at ease that dwells alone with neither gates nor bars; The cry at a nation's fall is heard as far as the Red Sea; God brings the four winds from the four ends of heaven to scatter a people; God sets his own throne in a conquered foreign land; Milcom (their 'king') dispossessed the tribe of Gad and will go into exile; Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, God will bring you down; Fire kindled in the wall of Damascus devours the palaces of Ben-hadad; God breaks the bow of Elam, the chief of their might; An envoy is sent among the nations to summon them to battle; Grape-gatherers would leave gleanings and thieves take only enough, but God strips the nation bare; The conqueror comes up like a lion from the jungle of the Jordan; and 7 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God points out his servant as unmatched on earth for piety (weight 7.7); God permits the adversary to afflict a righteous man, within set limits, to test his loyalty (weight 7.7); The Satan (the adversary) appears in the heavenly court as an accusing member (weight 7.1); A heavenly being reports he has been roaming to and fro on the earth (weight 7.1); The sons of God present themselves before YHWH in a heavenly assembly (weight 7.1); Men tear their garments in grief or dismay (weight 5.7). Only in Job's piety, the heavenly council and the first test: The verb 'bless' (barekh) used as a scribal euphemism for cursing God; Grown sons hold feasts in turn, each on his day, and invite their sisters; A great wind from the desert strikes the four corners of the house and it falls on the feasting children; God has set a protective hedge around the righteous man, his house and goods; 'Fire of God' falls from heaven and consumes flocks and servants; Messenger after messenger arrives while the last is still speaking, each the sole survivor of a disaster; 'Does he fear God for nothing?': piety suspected of being motivated by reward; The exemplary righteous man is a non-Israelite living in the land of Uz in the east; Father offers burnt offerings in case his children 'blessed' (cursed) God in their hearts; Mourner shaves his head and falls to the ground; A patriarch's wealth is listed in precise numbers of sheep, camels, oxen and asses; Humans are presented before God in rows, coming as they were first created; and 15 more.

Only in The second test; Job's wife; the three friends: 'Shall we accept the good from God and not accept the evil?'; The sufferer is struck with sore boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head; Mourners throw dust on their heads toward the sky; The sufferer sits among the ashes scraping himself with a potsherd; Comforters sit on the ground with the sufferer seven days and nights without speaking; Adversary's proverb 'skin for skin': a man gives all he has for his life; Three friends from distant places arrange to come together to console the sufferer; The sufferer's wife urges him 'Curse God and die'; How a worshipper responds to good fortune and to misfortune sent by God [contrast between the texts]; Friends see the sufferer from afar and do not recognize him; Seven days of mourning for the dead.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The woman falsely accuses the hero of assault (weight 6.6); Brothers, out of envy, plot to kill the hero (weight 6.6); Hero refuses, citing loyalty to his master and to God (weight 6.6); God's favor rests on the hero while he is a slave or prisoner (weight 6.6); Seduction attempt when the two are alone in the house (weight 6.4); The master's wife tries to seduce the hero (weight 6.1); Hero's beauty is remarked on (weight 5.5). Pair score 44.6.

Only in Joseph in Genesis (37, 39–50): After the father's death the brothers fear revenge; Grandfather crosses his hands to bless the younger first; Hero buys the people's land for the king during the famine; Father believes the hero is dead and refuses comfort; Father rebukes the hero for his dream but keeps it in mind; Father himself sends the hero to his brothers; Master entrusts his whole household to the hero; Father gives the hero a special garment; Hero accuses his brothers of being spies; Dream of the brothers' sheaves bowing to the hero's sheaf; Hero given an Egyptian priest's daughter as wife; Birds eat bread from on top of the dreamer's head; and 45 more.

Only in Tale of Two Brothers (Papyrus d'Orbiney 1,1-6,3): the household, the seduction and the false accusation: The woman makes herself look beaten (with fat and bandages), lies feigning sickness, does not pour water on her husband's hands or light the lamp, to support her accusation; In her false accusation the woman quotes her own proposal word for word as the hero's, and her own (fictive) refusal citing kinship; The false accuser tells her husband she will kill herself if he lets the accused live; The cattle speak to their herdsman and tell him where the pasture is good, and he understands them; Under the hero's care the master's cattle thrive exceedingly and multiply their calves; The hero runs away from his own brother, who pursues him to kill him; Refusing, the hero tells the woman she is like a mother to him and her husband like a father, and calls her proposal a great crime; The hero promises to tell no one of the woman's proposal and orders her never to speak of it again; The deceived husband (elder brother) sharpens his spear and waits behind the stable door to kill the hero on his return; The temptress promises the young man fine clothes as reward for lying with her; As each cow enters the stable it speaks to its herdsman, warning him that a man stands behind the door to kill him: 'flee!'; A tale opens with two brothers 'of one mother and one father', the elder a householder, the younger his helper; and 4 more.

Only in YHWH sayings and royal sayings (man plans, God disposes): By loyalty and faithfulness (hesed we-emet) iniquity is atoned for; When a man's ways please YHWH he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him; YHWH has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of evil; The worker's appetite works for him, for his mouth urges him on; The wrath of a king is messengers of death, but a wise man will pacify it; The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from YHWH; Divination (qesem) is on the lips of the king; his mouth does not err in judgment; Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones; Roll (commit) your works to YHWH and your plans will be established; The worthless man (ish beliyya'al) digs up evil and on his lips is a scorching fire; A whisperer separates close friends; In the light of the king's face is life; his favor is like a cloud of the latter rain; and 8 more.

Only in Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH: Bruising wounds scour away evil; blows cleanse the inner chambers; Bread gained by deceit is sweet, but afterwards the mouth is filled with gravel; 'Bad, bad,' says the buyer, then goes away and boasts; Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; a man of understanding draws it out; He who curses father or mother, his lamp is put out in the pupil of darkness; Many proclaim their loyalty, but a faithful man who can find?; The breath (nishmat) of man is the lamp of YHWH, searching all the inner chambers of the belly; A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them; It is a snare to say rashly 'Holy!' and only afterwards to reflect on vows; The glory of young men is their strength, the splendor of the old their grey hair; Wine is a mocker and strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by it is not wise; A king seated on the throne of judgment winnows all evil with his eyes; and 14 more.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Egypt is called 'the tents of Ham' or 'the land of Ham' (weight 7.3); Swarms (arov) of insects or wild beasts fill the houses of Egypt (weight 7.3); Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); God kills every firstborn of the land, from the king's heir to the lowest servant and cattle (weight 7.1); Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp (weight 7.1); A poetic list of the Egyptian plagues differs in number and order from Exodus (weight 7.1); Water brought out of a rock by the leader's rod (weight 7.1); Frogs swarm out of the river into houses, beds, ovens and kneading-troughs (weight 7.1); Nile water is turned to blood (weight 6.6); God rains bread from heaven to feed the people in the desert (weight 6.6); Psalm retells Israel's sacred history (patriarchs, Egypt, wilderness, conquest) as instruction or praise (weight 6.6); Locusts brought by an east wind devour all vegetation left after the hail (weight 6.5); God sends hail mingled with fire and thunder from heaven (weight 6.4); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 6.1). Pair score 96.2.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.

leads.summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window (weight 6.2); Hero singled out as righteous or pious (weight 6.2); Hero offers sacrifice after leaving the vessel (weight 6.2); Deity decides to destroy humankind (weight 6.1); All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8). Pair score 36.5.

Only in Ziusudra (Eridu Genesis, ETCSL 1.7.4, segments C-E): The flood storm rages for seven days and seven nights; A goddess laments the destruction of the people decreed by the gods; The sun god appears after the flood and shines into the boat through an opening the hero makes; Animals taken aboard (no pairing specified); The gods grant the flood hero life like a god, eternal life; The flood hero is settled in a far land (Dilmun) where the sun rises; The gods are made to swear an oath binding them to the decision to destroy humankind; Warning spoken to a wall or reed hut so the hero overhears; The verdict of the divine assembly to destroy is declared irrevocable; Seventh ancestor walks with God and is taken without dying; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; An oath sworn by the life of Heaven and the life of Earth; and 1 more.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer [divergence between the texts]; How the ark is described [divergence between the texts]; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; and 40 more.

leads.title: Dara Shikoh's Upanishads reach Schopenhauer
leads.summary: Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads into Persian as the Sirr-i Akbar (1657). Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version (Oupnek'hat, 1801–02) is how Schopenhauer read them.

passages.ref: Dara Shikoh, Sirr-i Akbar (1657); Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (1655)

evidence.text: Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn ('the meeting of the two seas') takes its title from Quran 18:60.

leads.title: Plotinus as the 'Theology of Aristotle'
leads.summary: An Arabic paraphrase of Plotinus' Enneads IV–VI circulated as the 'Theology of Aristotle' (al-Kindi's circle, 9th c.) and shaped Islamic Neoplatonism.

leads.title: Ancient treaty form and Deuteronomy's covenant
leads.summary: Deuteronomy follows the structure of ancient Near Eastern vassal treaties: preamble, history, stipulations, deposit, witnesses, curses and blessings.

evidence.text: Mendenhall (1954) argued for the Hittite model. Many scholars now consider Neo-Assyrian treaties the closer parallel. Which source is closer is the open question.
